Schema.Title: Arts/Crafts/Needlework
Schema.Definition: All products that are used to any creative activities that involve making things by hand or by using simple tools. Includes products for pottery, woodworking, jewelry-making, weaving, knitting, crochet, sewing, painting and sculpting.

Childs.Title: Arts/Crafts/Needlework Supplies
Childs.Definition: All products that are used to any creative activities that involve making things by hand or by using simple tools. Includes products for pottery, woodworking, jewelry-making, weaving, knitting, crochet, sewing, painting and sculpting.

Childs.Title: Artists Painting/Drawing Supplies
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that may be described/observed as supplies specifically designed for painting/drawing.

Childs.Title: Artists Brushes/Applicators
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as a device consisting of bristles or a piece of sponge-like material fastened to a handle and used by an artist to apply paint onto a surface such as paper or canvas. Includes products such as Artists Brushes, Applicators and Painting Knives.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Specifically excludes Household Paint Brushes classified in DIY. Excludes products such as Airbrushes and Sculpting Applicators.

Childs.Title: Type of Artists Brush/Applicator
Childs.Definition: Indicates, with reference to the product branding, labelling or packaging, the descriptive term that is used by the product manufacturer to identify the type of artist's brush or applicator.

Childs.Title: UNCLASSIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unable to be classified within their specific market; e.g. goat's cheese - goat's cheeses is often generically labelled and cannot be further classified.

Childs.Title: UNIDENTIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unidentifiable given existing or available product information.

Childs.Title: Artists Canvas/Pre-primed Boards
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as a surface used by an artist for painting, which may or may not be covered with a fabric such as canvas or hessian. Includes products such as Artists Stretched Canvas, Canvas Roll and Pre-Primed Boards.

Childs.Title: Magnifying Glasses
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as a portable, curved, single-lensed optical instrument, specifically designed to magnify vision, and typically intended to provide the user with an enhanced image of near objects and print.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as Binoculars, Monoculars, Telescopes and Microscopes.

Childs.Title: Microscopes
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as a multi-lens optical instrument designed to magnify vision and provide the user with a highly enhanced image of very small objects, which are often not visible to the naked eye. In order to view the objects, they need to be mounted on a prepared slide, which is placed under the lenses. These products typically have a scientific application.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as Binoculars, Magnifying Glasses, Monoculars and Telescopes.

Childs.Title: Monoculars/Telescopes
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as a cylindrical device containing a system of lenses and mirrors that collect and focus light to produce an image. They are specifically designed to magnify vision and intended to provide the user with an enhanced image of very distant objects. The image is viewed by one eye only. Products include hand held monoculars and astronomical telescopes mounted on tripods.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as Binoculars, Magnifying Glasses, Microscopes.

Childs.Title: Optics - Replacement Parts/Accessories
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as a replacement part or an accessory for products within the Optics class.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as Batteries and all Optics Products currently catered for in the Optics class.

Childs.Title: Optics Other
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as Optics products, where the user of the schema is not able to classify the products in any existing bricks within the schema.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes all currently classified Optics products as well as Interchangeable Lenses to be found in the photography class.

Childs.Title: Optics Variety Packs
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as two or more distinct Optics products sold together, which exist within the schema belonging to different bricks but to the same class, that is two or more products contained within the same pack which cross bricks within the Optics class. Includes products such as Binoculars and Magnifying Glasses sold together. Items that are received free with purchases should be removed from the classification decision-making process.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as Telescope and Astrology Chart Variety Packs.

Childs.Title: Analogue Cameras
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as an analogue device specifically designed to produce a permanent image of a person, location or event. Typically it is composed of a lens system contained within a lightproof box or compartment containing a light sensitive film that is positioned behind a shutter, so that when the shutter is opened/released an image is captured upon the film. The film is replaceable and can be exchanged for a new one once all the film has been exposed.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as Digital Cameras.

These products may be describe with characteristics of strengthening nails, preventing nails from being stained by nail polish colours, filling ridges, restoring moisture to the nail, and/or help polish adhere to the nail.

Childs.Title: NAIL TOP COAT
Childs.Definition: Nail Top Coat indicates the descriptive term used by the product manufacturer to identify the type of nail polish that is a clear coloured polish formula that is used specifically after applying nail polish to the nail. It forms a hardened barrier for the nail that can prevent chipping, scratching and peeling. Many top coats are marketed as "quick-drying" and/or helping the underlying polish to dry quickly.

Childs.Definition: Plastic is a material consisting of any of a wide range of synthetic or semi-synthetic organics that are malleable and can be molded into solid objects of diverse shapes. They are usually synthetic, most commonly derived from petrochemicals, but many are partially natural. The resulting powder, when mixed with water, will become a hydrated solid over time; used with water and sand or gravel to make concrete and mortar. Includes Portland cement and plastic cement to which a plasticising material (limestone or hydrated lime), as well as other materials has been added to reduce setting time and facilitate workability.

These products must be used whenever concrete is exposed to freezing and thawing, as well as to de-icing salts.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes concrete dyes and bonding agents.

Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes concrete mixes and agents as well as concrete dyes and training agents.

Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes concrete mixes, training agents and binding agents as well as floor paints.

Childs.Definition: Plastic is a material consisting of any of a wide range of synthetic or semi-synthetic organics that are malleable and can be molded into solid objects of diverse shapes. They are usually synthetic, most commonly derived from petrochemicals, but many are partially natural. Plasticity is the general property of all materials that are able to irreversibly deform without breaking, but this occurs to such a degree with this class of moldable polymers that their name is an emphasis on this ability.

Childs.Title: PLASTIC
Childs.Definition: Plastic is a material consisting of any of a wide range of synthetic or semi-synthetic organics that are malleable and can be molded into solid objects of diverse shapes. Plastics are typically organic polymers of high molecular mass, but they often contain other substances. They are usually synthetic, most commonly derived from petrochemicals, but many are partially natural. Childs.Title: PLASTIC
Childs.Definition: Plastic is a material consisting of any of a wide range of synthetic or semi-synthetic organics that are malleable and can be molded into solid objects of diverse shapes. Plastics are typically organic polymers of high molecular mass, but they often contain other substances. They are usually synthetic, most commonly derived from petrochemicals, but many are partially natural. Plasticity is the general property of all materials that are able to irreversibly deform without breaking, but this occurs to such a degree with this class of moldable polymers that their name is an emphasis on this ability.

They are usually synthetic, most commonly derived from petrochemicals, but many are partially natural. Plasticity is the general property of all materials that are able to irreversibly deform without breaking, but this occurs to such a degree with this class of moldable polymers that their name is an emphasis on this ability.

Childs.Title: PLASTIC
Childs.Definition: Plastic is a material consisting of any of a wide range of synthetic or semi-synthetic organics that are malleable and can be molded into solid objects of diverse shapes. Plastics are typically organic polymers of high molecular mass, but they often contain other substances. They are usually synthetic, most commonly derived from petrochemicals, but many are partially natural. Plasticity is the general property of all materials that are able to irreversibly deform without breaking, but this occurs to such a degree with this class of moldable polymers that their name is an emphasis on this ability.

Childs.Title: Window Locks/Bolts

Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as car window locks, door locks.

Childs.Title: Window Operators

Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes window handles, hooks and other accessories.

Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes all currently classified window replacement parts or accessories.

Childs.Title: Window Parts/Accessories Variety Packs

Includes products such as Window locks sold with Window handles. Items received free with purchases should be removed from the classification decision-making process.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes window parts and accessories that are sold individually.

A window shutter is an accessory featuring flat, louvred or corrugated panels that may be singular or paired and are attached to the exterior or interior frame of a window. It only concerns the motorisation mechanism as a separate item.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes window shutters.

Childs.Title: Window Shutters
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that may be described/observed as a window accessory featuring flat, louvred or corrugated panels that may be singular or paired and are attached to the exterior or interior frame of a window. Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as exterior trim veneers and exterior trim corbels and pediments as well as Window Shutter Motorisation.

Childs.Title: PLASTIC
Childs.Definition: Plastic is a material consisting of any of a wide range of synthetic or semi-synthetic organics that are malleable and can be molded into solid objects of diverse shapes. Plastics are typically organic polymers of high molecular mass, but they often contain other substances. They are usually synthetic, most commonly derived from petrochemicals, but many are partially natural. Plasticity is the general property of all materials that are able to irreversibly deform without breaking, but this occurs to such a degree with this class of moldable polymers that their name is an emphasis on this ability.

Childs.Title: PLASTIC
Childs.Definition: Plastic is a material consisting of any of a wide range of synthetic or semi-synthetic organics that are malleable and can be molded into solid objects of diverse shapes. Plastics are typically organic polymers of high molecular mass, but they often contain other substances. They are usually synthetic, most commonly derived from petrochemicals, but many are partially natural. Plasticity is the general property of all materials that are able to irreversibly deform without breaking, but this occurs to such a degree with this class of moldable polymers that their name is an emphasis on this ability.

They are typically intended to provide a disposable receptacle that may be discarded along with its contents when full. Includes products such as household bin liners in a variety of sizes.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as disposable food storage bags and all bags not intended to contain household and/or garden refuse.

Childs.Definition: Indicates, with reference to the product branding, labelling or packaging, the descriptive term that is used by the product manufacturer to identify if the product is scented.

Childs.Title: UNIDENTIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unidentifiable given existing or available product information.

Childs.Title: Type of Refuse Bag
Childs.Definition: Indicates, with reference to the product branding, labelling or packaging, the descriptive term that is used by the product manufacturer to identify different types of refuse bags.

Childs.Title: Waste Storage Products - Other
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as Waste Storage products, where the user of the schema is not able to classify the products in existing bricks within the schema.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes all currently classified Waste Storage products, Baby Hygiene and Grooming products and Baby Furniture and Transportation products.

Childs.Title: Waste Storage Products - Replacement Parts
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as replacement parts for Waste Storage Products.Includes products such as replacement parts for bin.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as Waste Storage products currently catered for within the Waste Management Products class.

Childs.Title: Waste Storage Products Variety Packs
Childs.Definition: Includes any products than can be described/observed as two or more distinct Waste Storage Products products sold together, which exist within the schema belonging to different bricks but to the same class, that is two or more products contained within the same pack which cross bricks within the Waste Storage Products class. Includes products such as diaper disposal bag and dustbin sold together. Items that are received free with purchases should be removed from the classification decision-making process.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as Baby Bottles with diaper disposal variety packs.

Childs.Title: PLASTIC
Childs.Definition: Plastic is a material consisting of any of a wide range of synthetic or semi-synthetic organics that are malleable and can be molded into solid objects of diverse shapes. Plastics are typically organic polymers of high molecular mass, but they often contain other substances. They are usually synthetic, most commonly derived from petrochemicals, but many are partially natural. Plasticity is the general property of all materials that are able to irreversibly deform without breaking, but this occurs to such a degree with this class of moldable polymers that their name is an emphasis on this ability.

Childs.Title: PLASTIC

Plastics are typically organic polymers of high molecular mass, but they often contain other substances. Childs.Title: PLASTIC
Childs.Definition: Plastic is a material consisting of any of a wide range of synthetic or semi-synthetic organics that are malleable and can be molded into solid objects of diverse shapes. Plastics are typically organic polymers of high molecular mass, but they often contain other substances. They are usually synthetic, most commonly derived from petrochemicals, but many are partially natural. Plasticity is the general property of all materials that are able to irreversibly deform without breaking, but this occurs to such a degree with this class of moldable polymers that their name is an emphasis on this ability.

Includes products such as power splitters, RF (radio frequency) signal splitters and microphone splitters.

Childs.Title: Surge Suppressors/Protectors
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as a device used to protect electrical appliances and electronic equipment. Surge protectors regulate the voltage supplied to an electric device by either blocking, or shorting to ground, voltage above a safe threshold. Includes products such as external surge suppressors, which are installed on the electrical panel to protect home appliances such as refrigerators and washing machines, or point-of-use surge suppressors, which are connected to individual pieces of home electronic equipment such as computers and televisions.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as circuit breakers and fuses.

Childs.Title: Switches

The flow is controlled by either turning the electricity on or off or by changing the path along which it flows and can be managed mechanically, electronically by remote control or via an app (smarthome).
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as dimmers classified with electrical lighting, relays and circuit breakers.

Childs.Title: Terminal Blocks/Strips
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as an insulating mounting for terminal connections. These products provide a convenient way to make temporary but secure electrical connections between wire and components. A raised ridge between the terminal points prevents arc-over between wires, as it ensures the frayed ends of stranded wires are kept in their proper place.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Specifically excludes products such as lugs, crimps and splicers. Excludes products such as Junction Boxes, Distribution Boards/Boxes and Surge Suppressors/Protectors.

Childs.Title: Charge/Voltage Regulators
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as a device that regulates the voltage and current coming from solar panels or other renewable energy sources to prevent damage to batteries and other energy storage systems. Charge controllers are typically used in off-grid or hybrid systems, where energy is generated from solar panels or wind turbines and stored in batteries for later use. The charge controller is responsible for managing the flow of energy between the renewable energy source, the battery bank, and the load to ensure that the battery is charged efficiently and effectively while also preventing overcharging and undercharging.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as converters, inverters and transformers.

Childs.Title: Electrical Generation Accessories/Fittings
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as an accessory or fitting used to assist or enhance the installation of electrical generation products. Includes products such as solar racking systems.

Childs.Title: Generators
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that may be described/observed as a machine that transforms mechanical energy into electricity. It consists of a magnet rotating in a coil wire, which frees electrons and pushes them along the wire.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes any other type of generators.

Childs.Title: Inverters
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as an electronic device that converts direct current (DC) electricity into alternating current (AC) electricity. In renewable energy systems, inverters are commonly used to convert the DC electricity produced by solar panels or wind turbines into AC electricity that can be used to power homes and businesses. Inverters are essential for renewable energy systems, as most electrical devices require AC power to function. In addition to converting DC to AC, inverters may also perform other functions, such as regulating the voltage and frequency of the AC output, providing grid-tie capabilities, and managing power quality.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as converters, charge/voltage regulators and transformers.

Childs.Title: Power Generator Set
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as a device which includes a power generator, an engine or motor that drives the generator, and any necessary ancillary equipment such as fuel tanks, control systems, and cooling systems. The system is designed to convert the chemical energy stored in a fuel source, such as diesel, natural gas, or gasoline, into electrical energy through a generator. Generator sets are commonly used for backup power, primary power, and mobile power applications in a wide range of industries and settings, including commercial, industrial, residential, and remote or off-grid locations. The size and configuration of a generator set can vary widely, from small portable units that can power a single device or system to large stationary units that can power entire buildings or facilities.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes all fuels and generators.

Childs.Title: Solar Panels
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as a device that converts sunlight into electricity through the photovoltaic effect. It is typically made up of multiple solar cells that are connected together and encased in a protective material, such as glass or plastic. The solar panel is designed to capture the energy from the sun's rays and transform it into electrical energy, which can be used to power a variety of devices.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as solar panel stations.

Childs.Title: Solar Power Stations
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/obseved as an easy to install kit consisting of a high power solar panel, battery, charge controller and inverter. The power station can power most appliances found in the home, office and workplace - such as TV's, stereo's, games consoles, lap top's, fax and power tools.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes all gas and electric powered heaters and solar panels.

Childs.Title: Water Turbines
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as a device that converts the potential energy of water into mechanical energy, which can be used to drive a generator that produces electrical energy. Water turbines are typically used in hydroelectric power plants, where they are placed in the flow of a river or other body of water to harness the energy of falling or flowing water. Water turbines can vary in size, from small turbines that are used to power individual homes or small businesses to large turbines that are part of hydroelectric dams that generate electricity for the grid.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as wind turbines and solar panels.

Childs.Title: Wind Turbines
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as a device that converts the kinetic energy of wind into electrical energy. Wind turbines consist of rotor blades attached to a central hub, which is connected to a generator that produces electricity. As the wind blows, the rotor blades spin, which in turn rotates the generator, producing electrical energy. Wind turbines can vary in size, from small turbines that are used to power individual homes or small businesses to large turbines that are part of wind farms that generate electricity for the grid.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as water turbines and solar panels.

Includes analogue and digital circuits.

They are usually synthetic, most commonly derived from petrochemicals, but many are partially natural. Plasticity is the general property of all materials that are able to irreversibly deform without breaking, but this occurs to such a degree with this class of moldable polymers that their name is an emphasis on this ability.

Childs.Title: Gases Not Used As Fuels
Childs.Definition: Gases that are used in items and are not used as a combustible fuel source.

Childs.Title: Technical Gases
Childs.Definition: Technical gases are a group of gases that are specifically manufactured for use in a wide range of industries.

Childs.Title: Carbon Dioxide Gas
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as carbon dioxide (CO2). CO2 is used as a pressurising agent for items such as beverages or model/remote control vehicles, and pellet/paintball guns.

Childs.Title: Helium Gas
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as Helium (He). "He" is used for items such as balloons, and some scuba applications.

Childs.Title: Nitrogen Gas
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as Nitrogen (N2). Nitrogen can be used for pressurising tyres.

Childs.Title: Nitrous Oxide Gas
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as a food additive version of nitrous oxide (N2O). N2O is used as a pressurising agent for items such as whipping cream canisters.

Childs.Title: Technical Gases Other
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as Technical Gases where the user of the schema is not able to classify the products in existing bricks within the schema.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes Carbon Dioxide Gas, Nitrogen, Nitrous Oxide Gas, and Helium Gas.

Childs.Title: Animal-derived Edible Products
Childs.Definition: Animal-derived edible products used for human consumption and sourced from various animals such as, swiftlet birds, equine donkey or other animal-derived products, where the user of the schema is not able to classify the products in existing bricks within the schema. Excludes animal-derived edible products used for human consumption such as eggs, milk, honey or other animal-derived products, where the user of the schema is able to classify the products in existing bricks within the schema.

Childs.Title: Animal-derived Edible Products - Prepared/Processed
Childs.Definition: Edible animal-derived products, which are used for human consumption that has gone through further manufacturing processes, such as reformed, cooked, dried, ground, cured or salted. Excludes animal-derived edible products prepared/processed, used for human consumption such as eggs, milk or honey or other animal-derived products, where the user of the schema is able to classify the products in existing bricks within the schema.

Childs.Title: Edible Bird Nest - Prepared/Processed
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed  as edible bird's nest, derived from the nests constructed by certain species of swiftlet birds, primarily Aerodramus fuciphagus. These nests, composed of the birds' saliva, are harvested and has gone through further manufacturing processes for culinary use. These products are typically consumed in soups, desserts, or tonics and are valued for their unique texture and potential health benefits.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as unprepared and unprocessed edible bird nest.

Childs.Title: Edible Donkey-hide Gelatin - Prepared/Processed
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as donkey-hide gelatin, made by boiling after removing the wool from the skin of the equine donkey. These products may vary in form and application, serving culinary purposes within Chinese cultural practices.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as unprepared and unprocessed edible donkey-hide gelatin.

Childs.Title: Animal-derived Edible Products - Unprepared/Unprocessed
Childs.Definition: Edible animal-derived products, which are used for human consumption that has not gone through any further manufacturing processes, such as reformed, cooked, dried, ground, cured or salted. Excludes animal-derived edible products unprepared/unprocessed, used for human consumption such as eggs, milk or honey or other animal-derived products, where the user of the schema is able to classify the products in existing bricks within the schema.

Childs.Title: Edible Bird Nest - Unprepared/Unprocessed
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed  as edible bird's nest, derived from the nests constructed by certain species of swiftlet birds, primarily Aerodramus fuciphagus. These nests, composed of the birds' saliva, are in their natural state and have not been subjected to any further manufacturing process. These products are typically consumed in soups, desserts, or tonics and are valued for their unique texture and potential health benefits.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as prepared and processed edible bird nest.

Childs.Title: Alcohol Flavouring Kit
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as a kit to add flavour to alcohol (generally spirits). These products are total units that include all or most of the necessary ingredients and/or equipment required to produce various flavours of beer, wine or spirits.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as Alcohol Making Accessories sold separately, Non-Alcoholic Drink Making Kits and Pre-Made Alcohol.

Childs.Title: Alcohol Making Kits
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as an alcoholic drink making kit. These products are total units that include most of the necessary ingredients and equipment required to produce various flavours of beer, wine or spirits.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as Alcohol Making Accessories sold separately, Non-Alcoholic Drink Making Kits, Alcohol Flavouring Kits and Pre-Made Alcohol.

Childs.Title: Type of Alcohol Making Kit
Childs.Definition: Indicates, with reference to the product branding, labelling or packaging the descriptive term that is used by the product manufacturer to identify a particular type or variety of alcohol making kit.

Childs.Title: BOURBOULENC

Childs.Definition: Clairette is a light-coloured grape variety that grows throughout southern France.

Childs.Title: DELAWARE

Childs.Definition: Grenache blanc is a variety of white wine grape that is related to the red grape Grenache. It is mostly found in Rhone wine blends and in northeast Spain.

Childs.Definition: Koshu is a white wine grape variety that has been grown primarily in Yamanashi Prefecture of Japan.

Childs.Title: LOUREIRO

Childs.Title: MUSCAT BAILEY A
Childs.Definition: Muscat Bailey A is a red wine grape hybrid developed by Zenbei Kawakami (1868-1944) at the Iwanohara Winery in Niigata Prefecture.

Childs.Title: NIAGARA
Childs.Definition: Niagara grapes are a variety of the North American grape species Vitis labrusca and are used as table grapes and for wines, as well as jams and juice.

Childs.Title: PEDERNA
Childs.Definition: Pederna or Arinto is a white wine grape variety grown in the hot wine regions surrounding Lisbon on the central coast of Portugal.

Childs.Title: RYUGAN
Childs.Definition: Ryugan (also known as Senkoji, possibly the same as China's Longyan), is grown in small quantities, predominantly in Nagano Prefecture in central Honshu.

Childs.Title: SEZAO
Childs.Definition: Sezão, formerly known as Souzão, is a Portuguese wine grape that is used in the production of port wine and table wines.

Childs.Title: TAUBERSCHWARZ
Childs.Definition: Tauberschwarz is also known as Blaue Frankentraube, Blauer Hängling, Blaue Hartwegstraube, Grobrot, Häusler, Süßrot, Karmazyn and Viesanka.

Childs.Definition: Avesso is a white Portuguese wine grape planted primarily in the Minho region of Portugal.

Childs.Title: AZAL
Childs.Definition: Azal or Azal Branco is a green-skinned wine grape variety found predominantly in the Minho region of northwest Portugal, where it is the second most-planted grape after Loureiro.

Childs.Title: BLACK QUEEN

Childs.Title: BOURBOULENC
Childs.Definition: Bourboulenc is an ancient white wine grape variety grown mainly in southern France.

Childs.Title: CASTELAO
Childs.Definition: Castelão, also known as Periquita and João de Santarém, is a dark-skinned grape variety that is among the most planted in Portugal.

Childs.Title: CLAIRETTE
Childs.Definition: Clairette is a light-coloured grape variety that grows throughout southern France.

Childs.Title: DELAWARE
Childs.Definition: The Delaware grape is a cultivar derived from the grape species Vitis Labrusca or 'Fox Grape' which is used for the table and wine production.

Childs.Title: GRENACHE BLANC (GARNACHA BLANCA)
Childs.Definition: Grenache blanc is a variety of white wine grape that is related to the red grape Grenache. It is mostly found in Rhone wine blends and in northeast Spain.

Childs.Title: KOSHU
Childs.Definition: Koshu is a white wine grape variety that has been grown primarily in Yamanashi Prefecture of Japan.

Childs.Title: LOUREIRO
Childs.Definition: Loureiro or Loureira is a white wine grape cultivated in the northwest of the Iberian Peninsula. This includes Galicia, Spain and Minho, Portugal.

Childs.Title: MUSCAT BAILEY A
Childs.Definition: Muscat Bailey A is a red wine grape hybrid developed by Zenbei Kawakami (1868-1944) at the Iwanohara Winery in Niigata Prefecture.

Childs.Title: NIAGARA
Childs.Definition: Niagara grapes are a variety of the North American grape species Vitis labrusca and are used as table grapes and for wines, as well as jams and juice.

Childs.Title: PEDERNA
Childs.Definition: Pederna or Arinto is a white wine grape variety grown in the hot wine regions surrounding Lisbon on the central coast of Portugal.

Childs.Title: RYUGAN
Childs.Definition: Ryugan (also known as Senkoji, possibly the same as China's Longyan), is grown in small quantities, predominantly in Nagano Prefecture in central Honshu.

Childs.Title: SEZAO
Childs.Definition: Sezão, formerly known as Souzão, is a Portuguese wine grape that is used in the production of port wine and table wines.

Childs.Title: TAUBERSCHWARZ
Childs.Definition: Tauberschwarz is also known as Blaue Frankentraube, Blauer Hängling, Blaue Hartwegstraube, Grobrot, Häusler, Süßrot, Karmazyn and Viesanka.

Childs.Title: TEMPRANILLO (ARAGONEZ/TINTA DE TORO/TINTA DEL PAIS/TINTA RORIZ/TINTO FINO/ULL DE LLEBRE)
Childs.Definition: The red grape variety originates from Spain, where it has the name of Tempranillo, it is also known as Tinta Roriz in Portugal's Douro region.

Childs.Title: TINTA BARROCA
Childs.Definition: Tinta Barroca is a Portuguese red wine grape that is grown primarily in Portugal's Douro region with some plantings in South Africa and the Riverland wine region of Australia.

Childs.Title: TINTO CAO
Childs.Definition: Tinto Cão is a red Portuguese wine grape variety that has been grown primarily in the Douro region.

Childs.Title: TOURIGA FRANCA
Childs.Definition: Touriga Franca or Touriga Francesa is an important dark-skinned grape variety used in the production of Port and dry red wines from Portugal's Douro wine region.

Childs.Definition: Avesso is a white Portuguese wine grape planted primarily in the Minho region of Portugal.

Childs.Title: AZAL

Childs.Title: BLACK QUEEN
Childs.Definition: Black Queen is a Japanese hybrid grape variety,

Childs.Title: BOURBOULENC
Childs.Definition: Bourboulenc is an ancient white wine grape variety grown mainly in southern France.

Childs.Title: CASTELAO
Childs.Definition: Castelão, also known as Periquita and João de Santarém, is a dark-skinned grape variety that is among the most planted in Portugal.

Childs.Title: CLAIRETTE
Childs.Definition: Clairette is a light-coloured grape variety that grows throughout southern France.

Childs.Title: DELAWARE
Childs.Definition: The Delaware grape is a cultivar derived from the grape species Vitis Labrusca or 'Fox Grape' which is used for the table and wine production.

Childs.Title: GRENACHE BLANC (GARNACHA BLANCA)
Childs.Definition: Grenache blanc is a variety of white wine grape that is related to the red grape Grenache. It is mostly found in Rhone wine blends and in northeast Spain.

Childs.Title: KOSHU
Childs.Definition: Koshu is a white wine grape variety that has been grown primarily in Yamanashi Prefecture of Japan.

Childs.Title: LOUREIRO
Childs.Definition: Loureiro or Loureira is a white wine grape cultivated in the northwest of the Iberian Peninsula. This includes Galicia, Spain and Minho, Portugal.

Childs.Title: MUSCAT BAILEY A
Childs.Definition: Muscat Bailey A is a red wine grape hybrid developed by Zenbei Kawakami (1868-1944) at the Iwanohara Winery in Niigata Prefecture.

Childs.Title: NIAGARA
Childs.Definition: Niagara grapes are a variety of the North American grape species Vitis labrusca and are used as table grapes and for wines, as well as jams and juice.

Childs.Title: PEDERNA
Childs.Definition: Pederna or Arinto is a white wine grape variety grown in the hot wine regions surrounding Lisbon on the central coast of Portugal.

Childs.Title: RYUGAN
Childs.Definition: Ryugan (also known as Senkoji, possibly the same as China's Longyan), is grown in small quantities, predominantly in Nagano Prefecture in central Honshu.

Childs.Title: SEZAO
Childs.Definition: Sezão, formerly known as Souzão, is a Portuguese wine grape that is used in the production of port wine and table wines.

Childs.Title: TAUBERSCHWARZ
Childs.Definition: Tauberschwarz is also known as Blaue Frankentraube, Blauer Hängling, Blaue Hartwegstraube, Grobrot, Häusler, Süßrot, Karmazyn and Viesanka.

Childs.Title: TEMPRANILLO (ARAGONEZ/TINTA DE TORO/TINTA DEL PAIS/TINTA RORIZ/TINTO FINO/ULL DE LLEBRE)
Childs.Definition: The red grape variety originates from Spain, where it has the name of Tempranillo, it is also known as Tinta Roriz in Portugal's Douro region.

Childs.Title: TINTA BARROCA
Childs.Definition: Tinta Barroca is a Portuguese red wine grape that is grown primarily in Portugal's Douro region with some plantings in South Africa and the Riverland wine region of Australia.

Childs.Title: TINTO CAO
Childs.Definition: Tinto Cão is a red Portuguese wine grape variety that has been grown primarily in the Douro region.

Childs.Title: TOURIGA FRANCA
Childs.Definition: Touriga Franca or Touriga Francesa is an important dark-skinned grape variety used in the production of Port and dry red wines from Portugal's Douro wine region.

Childs.Title: BOURBOULENC
Childs.Definition: Bourboulenc is an ancient white wine grape variety grown mainly in southern France.

Childs.Title: CASTELAO
Childs.Definition: Castelão, also known as Periquita and João de Santarém, is a dark-skinned grape variety that is among the most planted in Portugal.

Childs.Title: CLAIRETTE
Childs.Definition: Clairette is a light-coloured grape variety that grows throughout southern France.

Childs.Title: DELAWARE
Childs.Definition: The Delaware grape is a cultivar derived from the grape species Vitis Labrusca or 'Fox Grape' which is used for the table and wine production.

Childs.Title: GRENACHE BLANC (GARNACHA BLANCA)
Childs.Definition: Grenache blanc is a variety of white wine grape that is related to the red grape Grenache. It is mostly found in Rhone wine blends and in northeast Spain.

Childs.Title: KOSHU
Childs.Definition: Koshu is a white wine grape variety that has been grown primarily in Yamanashi Prefecture of Japan.

Childs.Title: LOUREIRO
Childs.Definition: Loureiro or Loureira is a white wine grape cultivated in the northwest of the Iberian Peninsula. This includes Galicia, Spain and Minho, Portugal.

Childs.Title: MUSCAT BAILEY A
Childs.Definition: Muscat Bailey A is a red wine grape hybrid developed by Zenbei Kawakami (1868-1944) at the Iwanohara Winery in Niigata Prefecture.

Childs.Title: NIAGARA
Childs.Definition: Niagara grapes are a variety of the North American grape species Vitis labrusca and are used as table grapes and for wines, as well as jams and juice.

Childs.Title: PEDERNA
Childs.Definition: Pederna or Arinto is a white wine grape variety grown in the hot wine regions surrounding Lisbon on the central coast of Portugal.

Childs.Title: RYUGAN
Childs.Definition: Ryugan (also known as Senkoji, possibly the same as China's Longyan), is grown in small quantities, predominantly in Nagano Prefecture in central Honshu.

Childs.Title: SEZAO
Childs.Definition: Sezão, formerly known as Souzão, is a Portuguese wine grape that is used in the production of port wine and table wines.

Childs.Title: TAUBERSCHWARZ
Childs.Definition: Tauberschwarz is also known as Blaue Frankentraube, Blauer Hängling, Blaue Hartwegstraube, Grobrot, Häusler, Süßrot, Karmazyn and Viesanka.

Childs.Definition: The red grape variety originates from Spain, where it has the name of Tempranillo, it is also known as Tinta Roriz in Portugal's Douro region.

Childs.Title: TINTA BARROCA
Childs.Definition: Tinta Barroca is a Portuguese red wine grape that is grown primarily in Portugal's Douro region with some plantings in South Africa and the Riverland wine region of Australia.

Childs.Title: TINTO CAO
Childs.Definition: Tinto Cão is a red Portuguese wine grape variety that has been grown primarily in the Douro region.

Childs.Title: TOURIGA FRANCA
Childs.Definition: Touriga Franca or Touriga Francesa is an important dark-skinned grape variety used in the production of Port and dry red wines from Portugal's Douro wine region.

Childs.Title: Non Alcoholic Beverages Variety Packs - Not Ready to Drink
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as two or more distinct Non Alcoholic Beverages Not Ready to Drink sold together, which exist within the schema belonging to different bricks but to the same class, that is two or more products contained within the same pack which cross bricks within the Non Alcoholic Beverages - Not Ready to Drink class. Includes products such as powdered Malt and Milkshakes sold together. Items that are received free with purchases should be removed from the classification decision-making process.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as powdered Milkshakes and Sugar Candy variety packs.

Childs.Title: Sports Drinks - Rehydration (Not Ready to Drink)
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as a beverage, which contains carbohydrates and electrolytes, designed to accelerate rehydration of cells by osmosis, normally consumed after a sporting activity. These products require the addition of water or other liquids prior to consumption and may be sold in liquid, powder or granular form. Includes products of various flavours such as orange and lemon.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as Sports Drinks - Rehydration - Ready to Drink and all Stimulants/Energy Drinks.

Childs.Title: Method of Carbonation
Childs.Definition: Indicates, with reference to the product branding, labelling or packaging, the descriptive term that is used by the product manufacturer to identify the method of carbonation of packaged water as required by legal requirements, for example, Codex Alimentarius.

Childs.Title: DECARBONATED
Childs.Definition: Decarbonated water is water which, after treatment and packaging, has less carbon dioxide content than that at emergence and does not visibly and spontaneously give off carbon dioxide under normal conditions of temperature and pressure.

Childs.Title: FORTIFIED WITH CARBON DIOXIDE FROM ANOTHER ORIGIN
Childs.Definition: Water which, after possible treatment has been fortified by the addition of carbon dioxide from another origin rather than the original source of the water.

Childs.Title: FORTIFIED WITH CARBON DIOXIDE FROM THE SOURCE
Childs.Definition: Water which is fortified with carbon dioxide from the source to have more carbon dioxide content than that at emergence.

Childs.Title: NATURALLY CARBONATED
Childs.Definition: Naturally carbonated water is water which, after possible treatment, possible re-incorporation of gas from the same source and packaging, has the same content of carbon dioxide as that at emergence.

Childs.Title: NON CARBONATED
Childs.Definition: A non-carbonated water which by nature and after possible treatment and packaging, does not contain free carbon dioxide in excess of the amount necessary to keep the hydrogen carbonate salts present in the water dissolved.

Childs.Title: UNCLASSIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unable to be classified within their specific market; e.g. goat's cheese - goat's cheeses is often generically labelled and cannot be further classified.

Childs.Title: UNIDENTIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unidentifiable given existing or available product information.

Childs.Title: Seafood Variety Packs
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as two or more distinct Seafood Products sold together which exist within the schema but belong to different classes, that is two or more products contained within the same pack which cross classes within the Seafood Family. Includes products such as Shrimp and Cod variety packs and Crabsticks and Herring variety packs. Items that are received free with purchases should be removed from the classification decision-making process.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as Fish and Tartar Sauce variety packs and cockles and mussels variety packs.

Childs.Title: Shellfish Prepared/Processed (Frozen)
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as an aquatic animal whose external covering consists of a shell, as in oysters, clams, lobsters and crabs, that has gone through further manufacturing processes, such as reformed, cooked, dried and salted, however these products can also be coated, in sauce, stuffed or filled. Products include sea snails and molluscs. However products may contain a small quantity of vegetables such as those in a sauce or stuffing/filling. These products must be frozen to extend their consumable life.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as shellfish with additional vegetables, dough or grains, shelf stable and perishable prepared and processed shellfish, all unprepared and unprocessed shellfish. Specifically excludes products that have added ingredients included such as rice, couscous and pasta.

Childs.Title: "EXTRA" CLASS
Childs.Definition: Products in this class must be of superior quality. They must be characteristic of the variety and/or commercial type specified. Depending on the nature of the produce specific provisions can apply as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. They must be free from defects, with the exception of very slight superficial defects, provided these do not affect the general appearance of the produce, the quality, the keeping quality and presentation in the package.

Childs.Title: CLASS I
Childs.Definition: Products in this class must be of good quality. They must be characteristic of the variety and/or commercial type. There can be specific provisions, depending on the nature of the produce as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. Slight defects, however, may be allowed, provided these do not affect the general appearance of the produce, the quality, the keeping quality and presentation in the package:- a slight defect in shape- slight defects in colouring- slight skin defects.

Childs.Title: CLASS II
Childs.Definition: This class includes products that do not qualify for inclusion in a higher classes but satisfy the minimum requirements for this product as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. The following defects may be allowed, provided the produce retain their essential characteristics as regards the quality, the keeping quality and presentation:- defects in shape- defects in colouring- skin defects.

Childs.Title: Quality (UNECE Standard)
Childs.Definition: Indicates, with reference to the product branding, labelling or packaging, the descriptive term that is used by the product manufacturer to identify the quality classification or category according to Codex Alimentarius or UNECE standards. UNCLASSIFIED applies to fruits that are not yet packed (e.g. delivery of a grower to a pack house) or not qualified to be sold as fresh fruits in the target market since they do not meet the specifications required by legislation.

Childs.Title: "EXTRA" CLASS
Childs.Definition: Products in this class must be of superior quality. They must be characteristic of the variety and/or commercial type specified. Depending on the nature of the produce specific provisions can apply as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. They must be free from defects, with the exception of very slight superficial defects, provided these do not affect the general appearance of the produce, the quality, the keeping quality and presentation in the package.

Childs.Title: CLASS I
Childs.Definition: Products in this class must be of good quality. They must be characteristic of the variety and/or commercial type. There can be specific provisions, depending on the nature of the produce as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. Slight defects, however, may be allowed, provided these do not affect the general appearance of the produce, the quality, the keeping quality and presentation in the package:- a slight defect in shape- slight defects in colouring- slight skin defects.

Childs.Title: CLASS II
Childs.Definition: This class includes products that do not qualify for inclusion in a higher classes but satisfy the minimum requirements for this product as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. The following defects may be allowed, provided the produce retain their essential characteristics as regards the quality, the keeping quality and presentation:- defects in shape- defects in colouring- skin defects.

Childs.Title: Quality (UNECE Standard)
Childs.Definition: Indicates, with reference to the product branding, labelling or packaging, the descriptive term that is used by the product manufacturer to identify the quality classification or category according to Codex Alimentarius or UNECE standards. UNCLASSIFIED applies to fruits that are not yet packed (e.g. delivery of a grower to a pack house) or not qualified to be sold as fresh fruits in the target market since they do not meet the specifications required by legislation.

Childs.Title: "EXTRA" CLASS
Childs.Definition: Products in this class must be of superior quality. They must be characteristic of the variety and/or commercial type specified. Depending on the nature of the produce specific provisions can apply as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. They must be free from defects, with the exception of very slight superficial defects, provided these do not affect the general appearance of the produce, the quality, the keeping quality and presentation in the package.

Childs.Title: CLASS I
Childs.Definition: Products in this class must be of good quality. They must be characteristic of the variety and/or commercial type. There can be specific provisions, depending on the nature of the produce as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. Slight defects, however, may be allowed, provided these do not affect the general appearance of the produce, the quality, the keeping quality and presentation in the package:- a slight defect in shape- slight defects in colouring- slight skin defects.

Childs.Title: CLASS II
Childs.Definition: This class includes products that do not qualify for inclusion in a higher classes but satisfy the minimum requirements for this product as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. The following defects may be allowed, provided the produce retain their essential characteristics as regards the quality, the keeping quality and presentation:- defects in shape- defects in colouring- skin defects.

Childs.Title: Quality (UNECE Standard)
Childs.Definition: Indicates, with reference to the product branding, labelling or packaging, the descriptive term that is used by the product manufacturer to identify the quality classification or category according to Codex Alimentarius or UNECE standards. UNCLASSIFIED applies to fruits that are not yet packed (e.g. delivery of a grower to a pack house) or not qualified to be sold as fresh fruits in the target market since they do not meet the specifications required by legislation.

Childs.Title: "EXTRA" CLASS
Childs.Definition: Products in this class must be of superior quality. They must be characteristic of the variety and/or commercial type specified. Depending on the nature of the produce specific provisions can apply as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. They must be free from defects, with the exception of very slight superficial defects, provided these do not affect the general appearance of the produce, the quality, the keeping quality and presentation in the package.

Childs.Title: CLASS I
Childs.Definition: Products in this class must be of good quality. They must be characteristic of the variety and/or commercial type. There can be specific provisions, depending on the nature of the produce as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. Slight defects, however, may be allowed, provided these do not affect the general appearance of the produce, the quality, the keeping quality and presentation in the package:- a slight defect in shape- slight defects in colouring- slight skin defects.

Childs.Title: CLASS II
Childs.Definition: This class includes products that do not qualify for inclusion in a higher classes but satisfy the minimum requirements for this product as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. The following defects may be allowed, provided the produce retain their essential characteristics as regards the quality, the keeping quality and presentation:- defects in shape- defects in colouring- skin defects.

Childs.Title: CLASS II

UNCLASSIFIED applies to fruits that are not yet packed (e.g. delivery of a grower to a pack house) or not qualified to be sold as fresh fruits in the target market since they do not meet the specifications required by legislation.

Childs.Title: "EXTRA" CLASS
Childs.Definition: Products in this class must be of superior quality. They must be characteristic of the variety and/or commercial type specified. Depending on the nature of the produce specific provisions can apply as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. They must be free from defects, with the exception of very slight superficial defects, provided these do not affect the general appearance of the produce, the quality, the keeping quality and presentation in the package.

Childs.Title: CLASS I
Childs.Definition: Products in this class must be of good quality. They must be characteristic of the variety and/or commercial type. There can be specific provisions, depending on the nature of the produce as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. Slight defects, however, may be allowed, provided these do not affect the general appearance of the produce, the quality, the keeping quality and presentation in the package:- a slight defect in shape- slight defects in colouring- slight skin defects.

Childs.Title: CLASS II
Childs.Definition: This class includes products that do not qualify for inclusion in a higher classes but satisfy the minimum requirements for this product as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. The following defects may be allowed, provided the produce retain their essential characteristics as regards the quality, the keeping quality and presentation:- defects in shape- defects in colouring- skin defects.

Childs.Title: UNCLASSIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unable to be classified within their specific market; e.g. goat's cheese - goat's cheeses is often generically labelled and cannot be further classified.

Childs.Title: UNIDENTIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unidentifiable given existing or available product information.

Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Specifically excludes: Prepared/Processed or Unprepared/Unprocessed and Shelf Stable or Frozen Quinces.

Childs.Title: Insects Edible
Childs.Definition: Insect species used for human consumption. Common forms of consumption are whole insects or processed insects into a non‐recognizable form, such as powders or flour.

Childs.Title: Insects Edible - Prepared/Processed
Childs.Definition: Insect species used for human consumption that has gone through further manufacturing processes, such as reformed, cooked, dried, ground, cured or salted.

Childs.Title: Bees/Wasps/Ants - Prepared/Processed
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that may be observed/described as a food product intended for human consumption, containing/consisting of insects from the Hymenoptera order, that have been subjected to one or more further manufacturing processes such as being cooked, dried, cured, ground, or reformed. Includes products such as Western honey bee (Apis mellifera).
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as Unprepared and Unprocessed edible insects.

Childs.Title: Beetles - Prepared/Processed
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that may be observed/described as a food product intended for human consumption, containing/consisting of insects from the Coleoptera order, that have been subjected to one or more further manufacturing processes such as being cooked, dried, cured, ground, or reformed. Includes products such as Mealworm (Tenebrio molitor)​ and Lesser mealworms/Buffalo worms (Alphitobius diaperinus).
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as Unprepared and Unprocessed edible insects.

Childs.Title: Butterflies/Moths - Prepared/Processed
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that may be observed/described as a food product intended for human consumption, containing/consisting of insects from the Lepidoptera order,that have been subjected to one or more further manufacturing processes such as being cooked, dried, cured, ground, or reformed. Includes products such as Silkworm (Bombyx mori).
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as Unprepared and Unprocessed edible insects.

Childs.Title: Cicadas/Leafhoppers/Planthoppers - Prepared/Processed
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that may be observed/described as a food product intended for human consumption, containing/consisting of insects from the Hemiptera order, that have been subjected to one or more further manufacturing processes such as being cooked, dried, cured, ground, or reformed. Includes products such as Cicadas (Cicadidae).
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as Unprepared and Unprocessed edible insects.

Childs.Title: Dragonflies - Prepared/Processed
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that may be observed/described as a food product intended for human consumption, containing/consisting of insects from the Odonata order, that have been subjected to one or more further manufacturing processes such as being cooked, dried, cured, ground, or reformed. Includes products such as Dragonflies (Epiprocta) Damselflies (Zygoptera).
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as Unprepared and Unprocessed edible insects.

Childs.Title: Flies - Prepared/Processed
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that may be observed/described as a food product intended for human consumption, containing/consisting of insects from the Diptera order, that have been subjected to one or more further manufacturing processes such as being cooked, dried, cured, ground, or reformed. Includes products such as Black Soldier Fly (Hermetia illucens).

Childs.Title: Grasshoppers/Locusts/Crickets - Prepared/Processed

Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as Unprepared and Unprocessed edible insects.

Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as Unprepared and Unprocessed edible insects.

There can be specific provisions, depending on the nature of the produce as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. Slight defects, however, may be allowed, provided these do not affect the general appearance of the produce, the quality, the keeping quality and presentation in the package:- a slight defect in shape- slight defects in colouring- slight skin defects.

Childs.Title: CLASS II
Childs.Definition: This class includes products that do not qualify for inclusion in a higher classes but satisfy the minimum requirements for this product as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. The following defects may be allowed, provided the produce retain their essential characteristics as regards the quality, the keeping quality and presentation:- defects in shape- defects in colouring- skin defects.

Childs.Title: Quality (UNECE Standard)
Childs.Definition: Indicates, with reference to the product branding, labelling or packaging, the descriptive term that is used by the product manufacturer to identify the quality classification or category according to Codex Alimentarius or UNECE standards. UNCLASSIFIED applies to fruits that are not yet packed (e.g. delivery of a grower to a pack house) or not qualified to be sold as fresh fruits in the target market since they do not meet the specifications required by legislation.

Childs.Title: "EXTRA" CLASS
Childs.Definition: Products in this class must be of superior quality. They must be characteristic of the variety and/or commercial type specified. Depending on the nature of the produce specific provisions can apply as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. They must be free from defects, with the exception of very slight superficial defects, provided these do not affect the general appearance of the produce, the quality, the keeping quality and presentation in the package.

Childs.Title: CLASS I

Childs.Title: Spinach (Fresh)
Childs.Definition: This Class contains Spinach (Spinacia oleracea), an edible flowering plant in the family of Amaranthaceae. While native to central and south western Asia, it is commonly grown through out the world. It grows to a height of up to 30 cm long and 1-15 cm broad, with larger leaves at the base of the plant and small leaves higher on the flowering stem. Spinach has a high nutritional value and is extremely rich in antioxidants, especially when fresh, steamed, or quickly boiled. It is rich in vitamins.

These products are non animal based and an imitation of meat products, meant to simulate the taste and mouthfeel of real meat but are normally made from a combination of non animal based ingredients. Includes products such as soya, fungus, beans, lentils, peas and chickpeas based products. These products must be frozen to extend their consumable life.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes all meat-based products and any other protein rich products such as eggs and pulses that constitute the main recipe ingredients. Also excludes Meat Substitutes - Non Animal based perishable and shelf stable products and Meat Substitutes - Animal based frozen, perishable and shelf stable products.

Childs.Title: Alternative Meat/Poultry/Other Animals Species - Prepared/Processed
Childs.Definition: Includes products from a single kind of animal other than beef, beefalo/cattalo, bison, chicken, deer, duck, elk/wapiti, emu, frog, goose, guinea fowl, goat, horse, lamb, land snail, llama/alpaca, moose/elk, ostrich, pheasant, pork, Wild boar, quail, rabbit, hare, reindeer/caribou, rhea, squab/pigeon, turkey, veal or wild buffalo (e.g., crocodile, snake, cat, dog or turtle) that have been subjected to one or more further manufacturing processes such as being cooked, dried, cured, ground, or reformed.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Specifically excludes Meat/Poultry/Other Animal Sausages - Prepared/Processed. Excludes Alternative Meat/Poultry/Other Animal Species - Unprepared/Unprocessed and Insects Edible - Prepared/Processed.

Childs.Title: Anatomical Form
Childs.Definition: Describes the meat product in terms of whether it is the whole animal or part of the animal which has been cut such as the muscle, bone, organ, or fat.

Childs.Title: BONE
Childs.Definition: Rigid, ossified organs from the endoskeleton of vertebrates.

Childs.Title: CARCASS (NON-POULTRY)
Childs.Definition: Body of large, slaughtered animal after offal is removed that is typically sold at wholesale level.

Childs.Title: FAT
Childs.Definition: Lipid animal tissue that is solid at room temperature.

Childs.Title: FEET
Childs.Definition: Structure composed of bone, meat, nail, and skin that bears the weight of the animal.

Childs.Title: FOREQUARTER
Childs.Definition: The anterior portion of a large animal spilt carcass.

Childs.Title: HEAD
Childs.Definition: Structure typically composed of bone, brain, and sensory organs. Also used for the target area of the human body.

Childs.Title: HINDQUARTER
Childs.Definition: The posterior portion of a large animal spilt carcass.

Childs.Title: MIXED PARTS FOR GROUNDING/MINCING
Childs.Definition: Two or more product forms are combined to create a single product such as a sausage.

Childs.Title: NECK
Childs.Definition: Structure typically composed of bone, meat and skin that attaches the head to the thorax. Also apply as a target area in human body care.

Childs.Title: NOT APPLICABLE
Childs.Definition: Form of product is not revelevant; for products such as mechanically separated meat.

Childs.Title: TAIL
Childs.Definition: Structure composed of bone, meat and skin that is from an appendage at the rear of the animal. Also apply to fish and other shellfish.

Childs.Title: TENDONS
Childs.Definition: Fibrous connective tissue.

Childs.Title: UNCLASSIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unable to be classified within their specific market; e.g. goat's cheese - goat's cheeses is often generically labelled and cannot be further classified.

Childs.Title: UNIDENTIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unidentifiable given existing or available product information.

Childs.Title: WHOLE BIRD
Childs.Definition: Body of a bird after offal is removed.

Childs.Title: WHOLE MUSCLE - NON POULTRY MEAT PART/PIECE
Childs.Definition: Large, unsliced muscle cut or part separated from a carcass and typically sold to the end consumer.

Childs.Title: WHOLE MUSCLE - POULTRY PART
Childs.Definition: Large, unsliced muscle cut or part separated from a whole bird and typically sold to the end consumer.

Childs.Title: WHOLE MUSCLE - PRIMAL
Childs.Definition: Unsliced whole muscle cut first separated from a large animal carcass.

Childs.Title: WHOLE MUSCLE - RIB CUT
Childs.Definition: Muscle piece from the chuck, rib, plate, or belly containing rib bones.

Childs.Title: WHOLE MUSCLE - ROAST CUT
Childs.Definition: Flat muscle slice that is 5 cm. (2 in.) or more thick.

Childs.Title: WHOLE MUSCLE - SLICE/CUTLET CUT
Childs.Definition: Thin, flat muscle slice that is less than 2 cm. (3/4 in.) thick.

Childs.Title: WHOLE MUSCLE - STEAK/CHOP CUT
Childs.Definition: Flat muscle slice that is 2 to 4 cm. (3/4 to 1 1/2 in.) thick.

Childs.Title: WHOLE MUSCLE - SUB-PRIMAL
Childs.Definition: Unsliced whole muscle cut separated from a large animal primal cut.

Childs.Title: Level of Cooking
Childs.Definition: The extent to which heat is used to preserve product quality and maintain wholesomeness.

Childs.Title: BLANCHED
Childs.Definition: Product which has been quick-cooked and then chilled to stop the cooking process.

Childs.Title: FULLY COOKED
Childs.Definition: Product has been thermally treated so that it is ready to eat or to be heated and served.

Childs.Title: PARTIALLY COOKED
Childs.Definition: Product has been thermally treated but requires additional cooking before it is ready to eat.

Childs.Title: RAW/UNCOOKED
Childs.Definition: Product has not been thermally treated.

Childs.Title: UNCLASSIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unable to be classified within their specific market; e.g. goat's cheese - goat's cheeses is often generically labelled and cannot be further classified.

Childs.Title: Meat Shape
Childs.Definition: Describes the presentation of the meat and the way it has been cut such as diced, sliced, rolled or shredded and shaped into patties, loafs, nuggets or meatballs.

Childs.Title: BULK/UNSHAPED
Childs.Definition: Product with no defined shape such as bulk ground or paste-like product.

Childs.Title: CHUB/LOG
Childs.Definition: A large generally tubular shape of ground or chopped product.

Childs.Title: DICED/CUBE-SHAPED
Childs.Definition: A product that has been cut into somewhat uniformly sized small blocks.

Childs.Title: LINK (MEAT SHAPE)
Childs.Definition: A generally short, tubular shaped ground or chopped product with or without an edible casing.

Childs.Title: LOAF
Childs.Definition: A generally rectangular shaped ground or chopped product.

Childs.Title: MEATBALL
Childs.Definition: A generally spherical mass of ground meat.

Childs.Title: NATURAL CARCASS/PART/MUSCLE
Childs.Definition: Shape of a naturally occurring body part, muscle, bone, or offal.

Childs.Title: NATURAL MUSCLE - SPIRALLY SLICED
Childs.Definition: Natural-shaped whole muscle product cut spirally around the bone (e.g. a spirally sliced ham).

Childs.Title: NUGGETS
Childs.Definition: A shaped small mass of ground or chopped product.

Childs.Title: PATTY
Childs.Definition: A generally flat, formed serving of ground meat.

Childs.Title: PULLED
Childs.Definition: Cooked product separated or pulled apart along its natural seams or grain.

Childs.Title: ROLLED
Childs.Definition: A product that has been rolled around itself or other added products.

Childs.Title: ROPE/RING
Childs.Definition: A long, tubular shaped ground or chopped product with or without an edible casing where the ends of each segment touch (ring) or where the length is coiled (rope).

Childs.Title: SHREDDED
Childs.Definition: Pulled product that is further size-reduced. A trade item is referred to as "shredded" if the loose particles are in the form of cylinders, shreds, or strings.

Childs.Title: SLAB
Childs.Definition: Whole backrib, sparerib, or smoked belly such as unsliced bacon, shaped as a broad, flat, thick piece.

Childs.Title: STRIP (MEAT SHAPE)
Childs.Definition: A long and thin piece of muscle or bacon.

Childs.Title: UNCLASSIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unable to be classified within their specific market; e.g. goat's cheese - goat's cheeses is often generically labelled and cannot be further classified.

Childs.Title: UNIDENTIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unidentifiable given existing or available product information.

Childs.Title: Mechanical Processing
Childs.Definition: Treatments, other than those involving heat, to tenderize the product, separate meat from non-meat, or alter the product size and appearance.

Childs.Title: CHOPPED AND FORMED
Childs.Definition: Product has been chopped into irregularly sized pieces and reformed.

Childs.Title: GROUND/MINCED
Childs.Definition: Product that has been extruded under pressure through a sieve.

Childs.Title: MECHANICAL TENDERIZATION
Childs.Definition: Product has been tenderized mechanically by a process such as needle tenderization or table-top cubing.

Childs.Title: MECHANICALLY SEPARATED
Childs.Definition: Product with paste-like consistency created by separating meat from bone using high pressure.

Childs.Title: NO MECHANICAL PROCESSING
Childs.Definition: Product has not been mechanically processed (e.g., not ground or mechanically tenderized).

Childs.Title: UNCLASSIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unable to be classified within their specific market; e.g. goat's cheese - goat's cheeses is often generically labelled and cannot be further classified.

Childs.Title: UNIDENTIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unidentifiable given existing or available product information.

Childs.Title: Non-Thermal Preservation
Childs.Definition: Treatments other than those involving heat or refrigeration to preserve product quality and maintain wholesomeness.

Childs.Title: DRIED
Childs.Definition: Product is exposed to a drying process to remove nearly all moisture.

Childs.Title: DRY AGED
Childs.Definition: Product held for an extended period of time in a cooled environment to enhance flavour and reduce moisture content.

Childs.Title: IRRADIATED
Childs.Definition: Product is exposed to ionizing radiation to destroy microorganisms, bacteria, and viruses.

Childs.Title: NO NON-THERMAL PRESERVATION
Childs.Definition: Product has not been non-thermally processed (e.g., not smoked or cured).

Childs.Title: PICKLED
Childs.Definition: Product preserved by immersion in brine solution.

Childs.Title: SALTED/CURED
Childs.Definition: Product preserved using salt, sugar, or nitrate.

Childs.Title: SMOKED
Childs.Definition: Product partially or fully cooked using a smoking process.

Childs.Title: SMOKED/CURED
Childs.Definition: Product preserved using salt, sugar, or nitrate and partially or fully cooked using a smoking process.

Childs.Title: UNCLASSIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unable to be classified within their specific market; e.g. goat's cheese - goat's cheeses is often generically labelled and cannot be further classified.

Childs.Title: UNIDENTIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unidentifiable given existing or available product information.

Childs.Title: Primary Additive
Childs.Definition: The primary non-meat ingredient added to the product.

Childs.Title: BATTER
Childs.Definition: Product has a wet flour-based coating applied topically.

Childs.Title: BREADING
Childs.Definition: Product has a dry bread-based coating applied topically.

Childs.Title: CHEESE
Childs.Definition: Product has cheese or cheese flavouring added.

Childs.Title: FLAVOURED SOLUTION/MARINADE INCORPORATED
Childs.Definition: Product has a liquid-based flavouring added by needle injection or by vacuum tumbling.

Childs.Title: FLAVOURED SOLUTION/MARINADE INCORPORATED AND TOPICAL MARINADE
Childs.Definition: Product has a liquid-based flavouring added by needle injection or by vacuum tumbling and a liquid-based flavouring applied topically.

Childs.Title: FRUIT
Childs.Definition: Product has diced or pureed fruit added.

Childs.Title: GLAZING
Childs.Definition: Product has a glaze coating applied topically.

Childs.Title: SAUCE/GRAVY
Childs.Definition: Product has a thick, liquid-based flavoring applied topically.

Childs.Title: SEASONING
Childs.Definition: Product has a dry, nonbread-based coating of herbs and/or spices applied topically.

Childs.Title: STUFFING/FILLING
Childs.Definition: Product has a stuffing mechanically added to its centre or the product is wrapped around a filling.

Childs.Title: TOPICAL MARINADE
Childs.Definition: Product has a liquid-based flavoring applied topically.

Childs.Title: UNCLASSIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unable to be classified within their specific market; e.g. goat's cheese - goat's cheeses is often generically labelled and cannot be further classified.

Childs.Title: UNFLAVOURED SOLUTION INCORPORATED
Childs.Definition: Product has unflavoured solution added by needle injection or by vacuum tumbling.

Childs.Title: UNIDENTIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unidentifiable given existing or available product information.

Childs.Title: Refrigeration State
Childs.Definition: The preservation state or extent to which heat is removed to preserve product quality.

Childs.Title: BULK FROZEN
Childs.Definition: Product is frozen after packaging and maintained at not less than -12.0 °C or more than -2.0 °C at all times after freezing.

Childs.Title: CHILLED
Childs.Definition: Product maintained at not less than -2.0 °C or more than + 4.0 °C at all times following the post-slaughter chilling process.

Childs.Title: INDIVIDUALLY FROZEN WITH ICE GLAZING
Childs.Definition: Product pieces are individually frozen before packaging and maintained at -18 °C or less at all times after freezing. Product is misted at the start of the freezing process to create a glaze of ice to keep pieces from sticking together and to minimize freezer burn.

Childs.Title: INDIVIDUALLY FROZEN WITHOUT ICE GLAZING
Childs.Definition: Product pieces are individually frozen before packaging and maintained at -18 °C or less at all times after freezing.

Childs.Title: SHELF STABLE
Childs.Definition: Product does not require refrigeration to maintain quality.

Childs.Title: UNCLASSIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unable to be classified within their specific market; e.g. goat's cheese - goat's cheeses is often generically labelled and cannot be further classified.

Childs.Title: UNIDENTIFIED

Childs.Title: DOMESTICATED/FARM RAISED
Childs.Definition: Product was produced using domesticated stock and common husbandry practices.

Childs.Title: UNCLASSIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unable to be classified within their specific market; e.g. goat's cheese - goat's cheeses is often generically labelled and cannot be further classified.

Childs.Title: UNIDENTIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unidentifiable given existing or available product information.

Childs.Title: WILD/WILD CAUGHT
