Childs.Title: DOMESTICATED/FARM RAISED
Childs.Definition: Product was produced using domesticated stock and common husbandry practices.

Childs.Title: UNCLASSIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unable to be classified within their specific market; e.g. goat's cheese - goat's cheeses is often generically labelled and cannot be further classified.

Childs.Title: UNIDENTIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unidentifiable given existing or available product information.

Childs.Title: WILD/WILD CAUGHT
Childs.Definition: Product was harvested from wild populations.

Childs.Title: Horse - Prepared/Processed
Childs.Definition: Includes products from animals of the species Equus caballus (domestic horse) that have been subjected to one or more further manufacturing processes such as being cooked, dried, cured, ground, or reformed.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Specifically excludes Meat/Poultry Sausages - Prepared/Processed. Excludes Horse - Unprepared/Unprocessed.

Childs.Title: Anatomical Form
Childs.Definition: Describes the meat product in terms of whether it is the whole animal or part of the animal which has been cut such as the muscle, bone, organ, or fat.

Childs.Title: BONE
Childs.Definition: Rigid, ossified organs from the endoskeleton of vertebrates.

Childs.Title: CARCASS (NON-POULTRY)
Childs.Definition: Body of large, slaughtered animal after offal is removed that is typically sold at wholesale level.

Childs.Title: FAT
Childs.Definition: Lipid animal tissue that is solid at room temperature.

Childs.Title: FEET
Childs.Definition: Structure composed of bone, meat, nail, and skin that bears the weight of the animal.

Childs.Title: FOREQUARTER
Childs.Definition: The anterior portion of a large animal spilt carcass.

Childs.Title: HEAD
Childs.Definition: Structure typically composed of bone, brain, and sensory organs. Also used for the target area of the human body.

Childs.Title: HINDQUARTER
Childs.Definition: The posterior portion of a large animal spilt carcass.

Childs.Title: MIXED PARTS FOR GROUNDING/MINCING
Childs.Definition: Two or more product forms are combined to create a single product such as a sausage.

Childs.Title: NECK
Childs.Definition: Structure typically composed of bone, meat and skin that attaches the head to the thorax. Also apply as a target area in human body care.

Childs.Title: NOT APPLICABLE
Childs.Definition: Form of product is not revelevant; for products such as mechanically separated meat.

Childs.Title: TAIL
Childs.Definition: Structure composed of bone, meat and skin that is from an appendage at the rear of the animal. Also apply to fish and other shellfish.

Childs.Title: TENDONS
Childs.Definition: Fibrous connective tissue.

Childs.Title: UNCLASSIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unable to be classified within their specific market; e.g. goat's cheese - goat's cheeses is often generically labelled and cannot be further classified.

Childs.Title: UNIDENTIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unidentifiable given existing or available product information.

Childs.Title: WHOLE MUSCLE - NON POULTRY MEAT PART/PIECE
Childs.Definition: Large, unsliced muscle cut or part separated from a carcass and typically sold to the end consumer.

Childs.Title: WHOLE MUSCLE - PRIMAL
Childs.Definition: Unsliced whole muscle cut first separated from a large animal carcass.

Childs.Title: WHOLE MUSCLE - RIB CUT
Childs.Definition: Muscle piece from the chuck, rib, plate, or belly containing rib bones.

Childs.Title: WHOLE MUSCLE - ROAST CUT
Childs.Definition: Flat muscle slice that is 5 cm. (2 in.) or more thick.

Childs.Title: WHOLE MUSCLE - SLICE/CUTLET CUT
Childs.Definition: Thin, flat muscle slice that is less than 2 cm. (3/4 in.) thick.

Childs.Title: WHOLE MUSCLE - STEAK/CHOP CUT
Childs.Definition: Flat muscle slice that is 2 to 4 cm. (3/4 to 1 1/2 in.) thick.

Childs.Title: WHOLE MUSCLE - SUB-PRIMAL
Childs.Definition: Unsliced whole muscle cut separated from a large animal primal cut.

Childs.Title: BLANCHED
Childs.Definition: Product which has been quick-cooked and then chilled to stop the cooking process.

Childs.Title: FULLY COOKED
Childs.Definition: Product has been thermally treated so that it is ready to eat or to be heated and served.

Childs.Title: PARTIALLY COOKED
Childs.Definition: Product has been thermally treated but requires additional cooking before it is ready to eat.

Childs.Title: RAW/UNCOOKED
Childs.Definition: Product has not been thermally treated.

Childs.Title: Meat Shape

Childs.Title: BULK/UNSHAPED
Childs.Definition: Product with no defined shape such as bulk ground or paste-like product.

Childs.Title: CHUB/LOG
Childs.Definition: A large generally tubular shape of ground or chopped product.

Childs.Title: DICED/CUBE-SHAPED
Childs.Definition: A product that has been cut into somewhat uniformly sized small blocks.

Childs.Title: LINK (MEAT SHAPE)
Childs.Definition: A generally short, tubular shaped ground or chopped product with or without an edible casing.

Childs.Title: LOAF
Childs.Definition: A generally rectangular shaped ground or chopped product.

Childs.Title: MEATBALL
Childs.Definition: A generally spherical mass of ground meat.

Childs.Title: NATURAL CARCASS/PART/MUSCLE
Childs.Definition: Shape of a naturally occurring body part, muscle, bone, or offal.

Childs.Title: NATURAL MUSCLE - SPIRALLY SLICED
Childs.Definition: Natural-shaped whole muscle product cut spirally around the bone (e.g. a spirally sliced ham).

Childs.Title: NUGGETS
Childs.Definition: A shaped small mass of ground or chopped product.

Childs.Title: PATTY
Childs.Definition: A generally flat, formed serving of ground meat.

Childs.Title: PULLED
Childs.Definition: Cooked product separated or pulled apart along its natural seams or grain.

Childs.Title: ROLLED
Childs.Definition: A product that has been rolled around itself or other added products.

Childs.Title: ROPE/RING
Childs.Definition: A long, tubular shaped ground or chopped product with or without an edible casing where the ends of each segment touch (ring) or where the length is coiled (rope).

Childs.Title: SHREDDED
Childs.Definition: Pulled product that is further size-reduced. A trade item is referred to as "shredded" if the loose particles are in the form of cylinders, shreds, or strings.

Childs.Title: SLAB
Childs.Definition: Whole backrib, sparerib, or smoked belly such as unsliced bacon, shaped as a broad, flat, thick piece.

Childs.Title: STRIP (MEAT SHAPE)
Childs.Definition: A long and thin piece of muscle or bacon.

Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unable to be classified within their specific market; e.g. goat's cheese - goat's cheeses is often generically labelled and cannot be further classified.

Childs.Title: UNIDENTIFIED

Childs.Title: Mechanical Processing
Childs.Definition: Treatments, other than those involving heat, to tenderize the product, separate meat from non-meat, or alter the product size and appearance.

Childs.Title: CHOPPED AND FORMED
Childs.Definition: Product has been chopped into irregularly sized pieces and reformed.

Childs.Title: GROUND/MINCED
Childs.Definition: Product that has been extruded under pressure through a sieve.

Childs.Title: MECHANICAL TENDERIZATION
Childs.Definition: Product has been tenderized mechanically by a process such as needle tenderization or table-top cubing.

Childs.Title: MECHANICALLY SEPARATED
Childs.Definition: Product with paste-like consistency created by separating meat from bone using high pressure.

Childs.Title: ANDOUILLE
Childs.Definition: A spiced, heavily smoked pork sausage, distinguished in some varieties by its use of the entire gastrointestinal system of the pig.

Childs.Title: ASPIC PRODUCT
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe products that are set in aspic or a savoury gelatine, this excludes head cheese.

Childs.Title: BIERSCHINKEN/KRAKAUER
Childs.Definition: Bierschinken is a scalded sausage from a cured mixture of meat, lard and spices that incorporates at least 15% small cubes of pork fat or cooked ham. It is produced mainly in Germany and Austria.

Childs.Title: BLOOD SAUSAGE/BLACK PUDDING/BLOOD PUDDING
Childs.Definition: Blood sausage is made by cooking blood with a filler until it is thick enough to congeal when cooled. Typical fillers include meat, fat, suet, bread, sweet potato, barley and oatmeal, and different meat sources are used.

Childs.Title: BOCKWURST
Childs.Definition: A German-style sausage made from ground veal and pork, flavored with salt, white pepper and paprika.

Childs.Title: BOEREWORS
Childs.Definition: Boerewors is a South African sausage made from coarsely minced beef, sometimes combined with minced pork, lamb, or both and spices such as coriander seed, black pepper, nutmeg, cloves and allspice. The sausage is preserved with salt and vinegar and packed in sausage casings. Traditional boerewors is usually formed into a continuous spiral. It can also be dried into what is colloquially known as droe wors.

Childs.Title: BOLOGNA
Childs.Definition: Bologna is an American-style sausage similar to Italian mortadella that can be made out of either chicken, turkey, beef, or pork. It is finely chopped or ground and contains lard, but without any visible pieces of fat. It is packed into casings with a variety of shapes including ring, chub, loaf, or rope. It is cooked, sometimes smoked, and sold with the casing removed and ready to eat.

Childs.Title: BRATWURST
Childs.Definition: Bratwurst is a sausage composed of several kinds of finely chopped meat that is traditionally prepared by grilling.

Childs.Title: CERVELAT
Childs.Definition: Cervelat is a cooked sausage consisting of a mixture of different meat, bacon, and pork rind that is packed into zebu intestines, slightly smoked and then boiled. It is produced mainly in Switzerland and in parts of Germany.

Childs.Title: CHORIZO/CHOURICO/LONGANIZA
Childs.Definition: Chorizo is typically a fermented, cured, smoked sausage that has a distinctive smokiness and deep red color from dried, smoked red peppers. Chorizo originates from the Iberian Peninsula.

Childs.Title: COUNTRY/BREAKFAST
Childs.Definition: Country and breakfast sausage is made from whole muscle product that is fresh and not cured or smoked (also known as "Whole Hog" sausage). It is normally made from pork but sometimes from turkey or beef. It is chopped and packed into casings for links or shaped as patties and used as part of a traditional American breakfast cuisine.

Childs.Title: EXTRAWURST
Childs.Definition: Extrawurst is an finely emulsified sausage, commonly of Austrian or German origin, with added bacon, garlic, spices and often potato added as a starch. It is cooked and served cold.

Childs.Title: FLEISCHWURST
Childs.Definition: A German-type of pork sausage

Childs.Title: HEAD CHEESE
Childs.Definition: Head cheese is not a dairy cheese, but a terrine or meat jelly made with flesh from the head of a calf or pig, or less commonly a sheep or cow, and often set in aspic.

Childs.Title: ITALIAN SAUSAGE
Childs.Definition: A popular American-style sausage with traditional flavors and spices of Italy (fennel and/or anise). It is typically made from pork but sometimes from turkey or beef. Normally it is fresh but can be smoked. It is chopped and packed into casings for links, shaped as patties, or sold in loose bulk and used for stuffing, fillings and meat balls.

Childs.Title: JAGDWURST
Childs.Definition: A German cooked sausage made of lean beef and pork.

Childs.Title: KIELBASA
Childs.Definition: A traditional seasoned and gently smoked Polish sausage made from choice cuts of pork, and often mixed with a little beef or veal.

Childs.Title: KNOCKWURST
Childs.Definition: A short, plump sausage made from ground veal and pork with fresh garlic in hog casings. Aged over burning oak wood.

Childs.Title: LINGUICA
Childs.Definition: A Portuguese-style cured pork sausage seasoned with onions, garlic, and paprika.

Childs.Title: LIVERWURST/LIVER SAUSAGE/BRAUNSWEIGER
Childs.Definition: Liverwurst is a sausage containing about 10 to 20% liver, which gives a distinctive liver taste. Other ingredients are meat, fat, and spices such as ground black pepper, marjoram, allspice, thyme, ground mustard or nutmeg. Most liverwurst varieties are spreadable. Liverwurst is sold ready to eat, but it can be cooked further as well.

Childs.Title: LYONER
Childs.Definition: A German-type of pork sausage which is usually eaten cold

Childs.Title: MERGUEZ
Childs.Definition: Merguez is a red, spicy sausage from Algeria and Tunisia, North Africa. Merguez is flavoured with a wide range of spices, such as sumac for tartness, and paprika, cayenne pepper, or harissa, a hot chili paste, that gives it a red color. It is traditionally made fresh and eaten after grilling.

Childs.Title: MET(T)WURST
Childs.Definition: Mettwurst is a strongly flavoured German sausage made from raw minced meat, which is preserved by curing and smoking. The most common variety is soft and somewhat smoked but still soft and spreadable.

Childs.Title: MORTADELLA
Childs.Definition: Mortadella is a large Italian-type sausage or cold cut sausage made of finely hashed/ground heat-cured pork, which incorporates at least 15% small cubes of pork fat (principally the hard fat from the neck of the pig). It is delicately flavored with spices, including whole or ground black pepper, myrtle berries, nutmeg, coriander and pistachios and/or olives. In several Arab and Muslim countries, Mortadella is made from chicken, beef, or turkey.

Childs.Title: SALAMI
Childs.Definition: Salami is a cured sausage, fermented and air-dried, which can be stored at room temperature for periods of up to a year. Well known are Italian Salami, Hungarian Szalámi and Spanish Salchichón. Salami is cured in warm, humid conditions in order to encourage growth of the bacteria involved in the fermentation process. After fermentation,the sausage has to be dried.

Childs.Title: TEEWURST
Childs.Definition: Teewurst is a German sausage made from two parts of raw pork (and sometimes beef) and one part bacon, which are minced, seasoned, and typically packed in porous, artificial casings before being smoked over beech wood. The sausage is then aged for seven to ten days in order to develop its typical taste. Teewurst contains 30 to 40 percent fat, which makes it particularly easy to spread.

Childs.Title: THURINGER
Childs.Definition: A sausage from the German state of Thuringia made from finely minced pork, beef, or veal. It is seasoned with salt, pepper, caraway, marjoram, and garlic. Normally it is smoked and cured.

Childs.Title: WEISSWURST
Childs.Definition: Weisswurst is a traditional Bavarian sausage made from very finely minced meat and fresh bacon. It is an unsmoked sausage usually flavoured with parsley, lemon, mace, onions, ginger and cardamom. For consumption, the sausages are quickly boiled in water, resulting in a greyish-white colour when served.

Childs.Title: WIENER/VIENNA/FRANKFURTER (WURSTEL)/HOT DOG
Childs.Definition: A moist sausage of soft, even texture and flavor, often made from mechanically recovered meat or meat slurry. Most types are cured or sometimes smoked and may have the casing removed after the cooking process. Hot dogs are sold fully cooked and ready to eat, although they are usually warmed before serving.

Some sausages are cooked during processing and may be preserved by curing, drying in cool air, or smoking.

Childs.Title: Type of Sausage
Childs.Definition: Indicates, with reference to the product branding, labelling or packaging, the descriptive term that is used by the product manufacturer to identify the type of sausage.

Childs.Title: ANDOUILLE
Childs.Definition: A spiced, heavily smoked pork sausage, distinguished in some varieties by its use of the entire gastrointestinal system of the pig.

Childs.Title: ASPIC PRODUCT
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe products that are set in aspic or a savoury gelatine, this excludes head cheese.

Childs.Title: BIERSCHINKEN/KRAKAUER
Childs.Definition: Bierschinken is a scalded sausage from a cured mixture of meat, lard and spices that incorporates at least 15% small cubes of pork fat or cooked ham. It is produced mainly in Germany and Austria.

Childs.Title: BLOOD SAUSAGE/BLACK PUDDING/BLOOD PUDDING
Childs.Definition: Blood sausage is made by cooking blood with a filler until it is thick enough to congeal when cooled. Typical fillers include meat, fat, suet, bread, sweet potato, barley and oatmeal, and different meat sources are used.

Childs.Title: BOCKWURST
Childs.Definition: A German-style sausage made from ground veal and pork, flavored with salt, white pepper and paprika.

Childs.Title: BOEREWORS
Childs.Definition: Boerewors is a South African sausage made from coarsely minced beef, sometimes combined with minced pork, lamb, or both and spices such as coriander seed, black pepper, nutmeg, cloves and allspice. The sausage is preserved with salt and vinegar and packed in sausage casings. Traditional boerewors is usually formed into a continuous spiral. It can also be dried into what is colloquially known as droe wors.

Childs.Title: BOLOGNA
Childs.Definition: Bologna is an American-style sausage similar to Italian mortadella that can be made out of either chicken, turkey, beef, or pork. It is finely chopped or ground and contains lard, but without any visible pieces of fat. It is packed into casings with a variety of shapes including ring, chub, loaf, or rope. It is cooked, sometimes smoked, and sold with the casing removed and ready to eat.

Childs.Title: BRATWURST
Childs.Definition: Bratwurst is a sausage composed of several kinds of finely chopped meat that is traditionally prepared by grilling.

Childs.Title: CERVELAT
Childs.Definition: Cervelat is a cooked sausage consisting of a mixture of different meat, bacon, and pork rind that is packed into zebu intestines, slightly smoked and then boiled. It is produced mainly in Switzerland and in parts of Germany.

Childs.Title: CHORIZO/CHOURICO/LONGANIZA
Childs.Definition: Chorizo is typically a fermented, cured, smoked sausage that has a distinctive smokiness and deep red color from dried, smoked red peppers. Chorizo originates from the Iberian Peninsula.

Childs.Title: COUNTRY/BREAKFAST
Childs.Definition: Country and breakfast sausage is made from whole muscle product that is fresh and not cured or smoked (also known as "Whole Hog" sausage). It is normally made from pork but sometimes from turkey or beef. It is chopped and packed into casings for links or shaped as patties and used as part of a traditional American breakfast cuisine.

Childs.Title: EXTRAWURST
Childs.Definition: Extrawurst is an finely emulsified sausage, commonly of Austrian or German origin, with added bacon, garlic, spices and often potato added as a starch. It is cooked and served cold.

Childs.Title: FLEISCHWURST
Childs.Definition: A German-type of pork sausage

Childs.Title: HEAD CHEESE
Childs.Definition: Head cheese is not a dairy cheese, but a terrine or meat jelly made with flesh from the head of a calf or pig, or less commonly a sheep or cow, and often set in aspic.

Childs.Title: ITALIAN SAUSAGE
Childs.Definition: A popular American-style sausage with traditional flavors and spices of Italy (fennel and/or anise). It is typically made from pork but sometimes from turkey or beef. Normally it is fresh but can be smoked. It is chopped and packed into casings for links, shaped as patties, or sold in loose bulk and used for stuffing, fillings and meat balls.

Childs.Title: JAGDWURST
Childs.Definition: A German cooked sausage made of lean beef and pork.

Childs.Title: KIELBASA
Childs.Definition: A traditional seasoned and gently smoked Polish sausage made from choice cuts of pork, and often mixed with a little beef or veal.

Childs.Title: KNOCKWURST
Childs.Definition: A short, plump sausage made from ground veal and pork with fresh garlic in hog casings. Aged over burning oak wood.

Childs.Title: LINGUICA
Childs.Definition: A Portuguese-style cured pork sausage seasoned with onions, garlic, and paprika.

Childs.Title: LIVERWURST/LIVER SAUSAGE/BRAUNSWEIGER
Childs.Definition: Liverwurst is a sausage containing about 10 to 20% liver, which gives a distinctive liver taste. Other ingredients are meat, fat, and spices such as ground black pepper, marjoram, allspice, thyme, ground mustard or nutmeg. Most liverwurst varieties are spreadable. Liverwurst is sold ready to eat, but it can be cooked further as well.

Childs.Title: LYONER
Childs.Definition: A German-type of pork sausage which is usually eaten cold

Childs.Title: MERGUEZ
Childs.Definition: Merguez is a red, spicy sausage from Algeria and Tunisia, North Africa. Merguez is flavoured with a wide range of spices, such as sumac for tartness, and paprika, cayenne pepper, or harissa, a hot chili paste, that gives it a red color. It is traditionally made fresh and eaten after grilling.

Childs.Title: MET(T)WURST
Childs.Definition: Mettwurst is a strongly flavoured German sausage made from raw minced meat, which is preserved by curing and smoking. The most common variety is soft and somewhat smoked but still soft and spreadable.

Childs.Title: MORTADELLA
Childs.Definition: Mortadella is a large Italian-type sausage or cold cut sausage made of finely hashed/ground heat-cured pork, which incorporates at least 15% small cubes of pork fat (principally the hard fat from the neck of the pig). It is delicately flavored with spices, including whole or ground black pepper, myrtle berries, nutmeg, coriander and pistachios and/or olives. In several Arab and Muslim countries, Mortadella is made from chicken, beef, or turkey.

Childs.Title: SALAMI
Childs.Definition: Salami is a cured sausage, fermented and air-dried, which can be stored at room temperature for periods of up to a year. Well known are Italian Salami, Hungarian Szalámi and Spanish Salchichón. Salami is cured in warm, humid conditions in order to encourage growth of the bacteria involved in the fermentation process. After fermentation,the sausage has to be dried.

Childs.Title: TEEWURST
Childs.Definition: Teewurst is a German sausage made from two parts of raw pork (and sometimes beef) and one part bacon, which are minced, seasoned, and typically packed in porous, artificial casings before being smoked over beech wood. The sausage is then aged for seven to ten days in order to develop its typical taste. Teewurst contains 30 to 40 percent fat, which makes it particularly easy to spread.

Childs.Title: THURINGER
Childs.Definition: A sausage from the German state of Thuringia made from finely minced pork, beef, or veal. It is seasoned with salt, pepper, caraway, marjoram, and garlic. Normally it is smoked and cured.

Childs.Title: UNIDENTIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unidentifiable given existing or available product information.

Childs.Title: WEISSWURST
Childs.Definition: Weisswurst is a traditional Bavarian sausage made from very finely minced meat and fresh bacon. It is an unsmoked sausage usually flavoured with parsley, lemon, mace, onions, ginger and cardamom. For consumption, the sausages are quickly boiled in water, resulting in a greyish-white colour when served.

Childs.Title: WIENER/VIENNA/FRANKFURTER (WURSTEL)/HOT DOG
Childs.Definition: A moist sausage of soft, even texture and flavor, often made from mechanically recovered meat or meat slurry. Most types are cured or sometimes smoked and may have the casing removed after the cooking process. Hot dogs are sold fully cooked and ready to eat, although they are usually warmed before serving.

Childs.Title: Chicken Sausages - Prepared/Processed
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as a food made from ground chicken, which may be prepared using a specific, regionally based process. The ground meat is mixed with other ingredients such as animal fat, salt, spices, herbs, vegetables or fruit and then typically packed in a casing, which may be link shaped or form a rope or ring, or sold without a casing such as bologna and some frankfurters. Some sausages are cooked during processing and may be preserved by curing, drying in cool air, or smoking.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as vegetarian sausages made from meat substitutes as well as pate.

Childs.Definition: A short, plump sausage made from ground veal and pork with fresh garlic in hog casings. Aged over burning oak wood.

Childs.Title: LINGUICA
Childs.Definition: A Portuguese-style cured pork sausage seasoned with onions, garlic, and paprika.

Childs.Title: LIVERWURST/LIVER SAUSAGE/BRAUNSWEIGER
Childs.Definition: Liverwurst is a sausage containing about 10 to 20% liver, which gives a distinctive liver taste. Other ingredients are meat, fat, and spices such as ground black pepper, marjoram, allspice, thyme, ground mustard or nutmeg. Most liverwurst varieties are spreadable. Liverwurst is sold ready to eat, but it can be cooked further as well.

Childs.Title: LYONER
Childs.Definition: A German-type of pork sausage which is usually eaten cold

Childs.Title: MERGUEZ
Childs.Definition: Merguez is a red, spicy sausage from Algeria and Tunisia, North Africa. Merguez is flavoured with a wide range of spices, such as sumac for tartness, and paprika, cayenne pepper, or harissa, a hot chili paste, that gives it a red color. It is traditionally made fresh and eaten after grilling.

Childs.Title: MET(T)WURST
Childs.Definition: Mettwurst is a strongly flavoured German sausage made from raw minced meat, which is preserved by curing and smoking. The most common variety is soft and somewhat smoked but still soft and spreadable.

Childs.Title: MORTADELLA
Childs.Definition: Mortadella is a large Italian-type sausage or cold cut sausage made of finely hashed/ground heat-cured pork, which incorporates at least 15% small cubes of pork fat (principally the hard fat from the neck of the pig). It is delicately flavored with spices, including whole or ground black pepper, myrtle berries, nutmeg, coriander and pistachios and/or olives. In several Arab and Muslim countries, Mortadella is made from chicken, beef, or turkey.

Childs.Title: SALAMI
Childs.Definition: Salami is a cured sausage, fermented and air-dried, which can be stored at room temperature for periods of up to a year. Well known are Italian Salami, Hungarian Szalámi and Spanish Salchichón. Salami is cured in warm, humid conditions in order to encourage growth of the bacteria involved in the fermentation process. After fermentation,the sausage has to be dried.

Childs.Title: TEEWURST
Childs.Definition: Teewurst is a German sausage made from two parts of raw pork (and sometimes beef) and one part bacon, which are minced, seasoned, and typically packed in porous, artificial casings before being smoked over beech wood. The sausage is then aged for seven to ten days in order to develop its typical taste. Teewurst contains 30 to 40 percent fat, which makes it particularly easy to spread.

Childs.Title: THURINGER
Childs.Definition: A sausage from the German state of Thuringia made from finely minced pork, beef, or veal. It is seasoned with salt, pepper, caraway, marjoram, and garlic. Normally it is smoked and cured.

Childs.Title: WEISSWURST
Childs.Definition: Weisswurst is a traditional Bavarian sausage made from very finely minced meat and fresh bacon. It is an unsmoked sausage usually flavoured with parsley, lemon, mace, onions, ginger and cardamom. For consumption, the sausages are quickly boiled in water, resulting in a greyish-white colour when served.

Childs.Title: WIENER/VIENNA/FRANKFURTER (WURSTEL)/HOT DOG
Childs.Definition: A moist sausage of soft, even texture and flavor, often made from mechanically recovered meat or meat slurry. Most types are cured or sometimes smoked and may have the casing removed after the cooking process. Hot dogs are sold fully cooked and ready to eat, although they are usually warmed before serving.

Childs.Title: Lamb/Mutton Sausages - Prepared/Processed
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as a food made from ground lamb/mutton, which may be prepared using a specific, regionally based process. The ground meat is mixed with other ingredients such as animal fat, salt, spices, herbs, vegetables or fruit and then typically packed in a casing, which may be link shaped or form a rope or ring, or sold without a casing such as bologna and some frankfurters. Some sausages are cooked during processing and may be preserved by curing, drying in cool air, or smoking.

Childs.Title: ASPIC PRODUCT

Childs.Title: BIERSCHINKEN/KRAKAUER
Childs.Definition: Bierschinken is a scalded sausage from a cured mixture of meat, lard and spices that incorporates at least 15% small cubes of pork fat or cooked ham. It is produced mainly in Germany and Austria.

Childs.Title: BLOOD SAUSAGE/BLACK PUDDING/BLOOD PUDDING
Childs.Definition: Blood sausage is made by cooking blood with a filler until it is thick enough to congeal when cooled. Typical fillers include meat, fat, suet, bread, sweet potato, barley and oatmeal, and different meat sources are used.

Childs.Title: BOCKWURST
Childs.Definition: A German-style sausage made from ground veal and pork, flavored with salt, white pepper and paprika.

Childs.Title: BOLOGNA
Childs.Definition: Bologna is an American-style sausage similar to Italian mortadella that can be made out of either chicken, turkey, beef, or pork. It is finely chopped or ground and contains lard, but without any visible pieces of fat. It is packed into casings with a variety of shapes including ring, chub, loaf, or rope. It is cooked, sometimes smoked, and sold with the casing removed and ready to eat.

Childs.Title: BRATWURST
Childs.Definition: Bratwurst is a sausage composed of several kinds of finely chopped meat that is traditionally prepared by grilling.

Childs.Title: CERVELAT
Childs.Definition: Cervelat is a cooked sausage consisting of a mixture of different meat, bacon, and pork rind that is packed into zebu intestines, slightly smoked and then boiled. It is produced mainly in Switzerland and in parts of Germany.

Childs.Title: CHORIZO/CHOURICO/LONGANIZA
Childs.Definition: Chorizo is typically a fermented, cured, smoked sausage that has a distinctive smokiness and deep red color from dried, smoked red peppers. Chorizo originates from the Iberian Peninsula.

Childs.Title: COUNTRY/BREAKFAST
Childs.Definition: Country and breakfast sausage is made from whole muscle product that is fresh and not cured or smoked (also known as "Whole Hog" sausage). It is normally made from pork but sometimes from turkey or beef. It is chopped and packed into casings for links or shaped as patties and used as part of a traditional American breakfast cuisine.

Childs.Title: EXTRAWURST
Childs.Definition: Extrawurst is an finely emulsified sausage, commonly of Austrian or German origin, with added bacon, garlic, spices and often potato added as a starch. It is cooked and served cold.

Childs.Title: FLEISCHWURST
Childs.Definition: A German-type of pork sausage

Childs.Title: HEAD CHEESE
Childs.Definition: Head cheese is not a dairy cheese, but a terrine or meat jelly made with flesh from the head of a calf or pig, or less commonly a sheep or cow, and often set in aspic.

Childs.Title: ITALIAN SAUSAGE
Childs.Definition: A popular American-style sausage with traditional flavors and spices of Italy (fennel and/or anise). It is typically made from pork but sometimes from turkey or beef. Normally it is fresh but can be smoked. It is chopped and packed into casings for links, shaped as patties, or sold in loose bulk and used for stuffing, fillings and meat balls.

Childs.Title: JAGDWURST
Childs.Definition: A German cooked sausage made of lean beef and pork.

Childs.Title: Type of Sausage

Childs.Title: ANDOUILLE
Childs.Definition: A spiced, heavily smoked pork sausage, distinguished in some varieties by its use of the entire gastrointestinal system of the pig.

Childs.Title: ASPIC PRODUCT
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe products that are set in aspic or a savoury gelatine, this excludes head cheese.

Childs.Title: BIERSCHINKEN/KRAKAUER
Childs.Definition: Bierschinken is a scalded sausage from a cured mixture of meat, lard and spices that incorporates at least 15% small cubes of pork fat or cooked ham. It is produced mainly in Germany and Austria.

Childs.Title: BLOOD SAUSAGE/BLACK PUDDING/BLOOD PUDDING
Childs.Definition: Blood sausage is made by cooking blood with a filler until it is thick enough to congeal when cooled. Typical fillers include meat, fat, suet, bread, sweet potato, barley and oatmeal, and different meat sources are used.

Childs.Title: BOCKWURST
Childs.Definition: A German-style sausage made from ground veal and pork, flavored with salt, white pepper and paprika.

Childs.Title: BOEREWORS
Childs.Definition: Boerewors is a South African sausage made from coarsely minced beef, sometimes combined with minced pork, lamb, or both and spices such as coriander seed, black pepper, nutmeg, cloves and allspice. The sausage is preserved with salt and vinegar and packed in sausage casings. Traditional boerewors is usually formed into a continuous spiral. It can also be dried into what is colloquially known as droe wors.

Childs.Title: BOLOGNA
Childs.Definition: Bologna is an American-style sausage similar to Italian mortadella that can be made out of either chicken, turkey, beef, or pork. It is finely chopped or ground and contains lard, but without any visible pieces of fat. It is packed into casings with a variety of shapes including ring, chub, loaf, or rope. It is cooked, sometimes smoked, and sold with the casing removed and ready to eat.

Childs.Title: BRATWURST
Childs.Definition: Bratwurst is a sausage composed of several kinds of finely chopped meat that is traditionally prepared by grilling.

Childs.Title: CERVELAT
Childs.Definition: Cervelat is a cooked sausage consisting of a mixture of different meat, bacon, and pork rind that is packed into zebu intestines, slightly smoked and then boiled. It is produced mainly in Switzerland and in parts of Germany.

Childs.Title: CHORIZO/CHOURICO/LONGANIZA
Childs.Definition: Chorizo is typically a fermented, cured, smoked sausage that has a distinctive smokiness and deep red color from dried, smoked red peppers. Chorizo originates from the Iberian Peninsula.

Childs.Title: COUNTRY/BREAKFAST
Childs.Definition: Country and breakfast sausage is made from whole muscle product that is fresh and not cured or smoked (also known as "Whole Hog" sausage). It is normally made from pork but sometimes from turkey or beef. It is chopped and packed into casings for links or shaped as patties and used as part of a traditional American breakfast cuisine.

Childs.Title: EXTRAWURST
Childs.Definition: Extrawurst is an finely emulsified sausage, commonly of Austrian or German origin, with added bacon, garlic, spices and often potato added as a starch. It is cooked and served cold.

Childs.Title: FLEISCHWURST
Childs.Definition: A German-type of pork sausage

Childs.Title: HEAD CHEESE
Childs.Definition: Head cheese is not a dairy cheese, but a terrine or meat jelly made with flesh from the head of a calf or pig, or less commonly a sheep or cow, and often set in aspic.

Childs.Title: ITALIAN SAUSAGE
Childs.Definition: A popular American-style sausage with traditional flavors and spices of Italy (fennel and/or anise). It is typically made from pork but sometimes from turkey or beef. Normally it is fresh but can be smoked. It is chopped and packed into casings for links, shaped as patties, or sold in loose bulk and used for stuffing, fillings and meat balls.

Childs.Title: JAGDWURST
Childs.Definition: A German cooked sausage made of lean beef and pork.

Childs.Title: KIELBASA
Childs.Definition: A traditional seasoned and gently smoked Polish sausage made from choice cuts of pork, and often mixed with a little beef or veal.

Childs.Title: KNOCKWURST
Childs.Definition: A short, plump sausage made from ground veal and pork with fresh garlic in hog casings. Aged over burning oak wood.

Childs.Title: LINGUICA
Childs.Definition: A Portuguese-style cured pork sausage seasoned with onions, garlic, and paprika.

Childs.Title: LIVERWURST/LIVER SAUSAGE/BRAUNSWEIGER
Childs.Definition: Liverwurst is a sausage containing about 10 to 20% liver, which gives a distinctive liver taste. Other ingredients are meat, fat, and spices such as ground black pepper, marjoram, allspice, thyme, ground mustard or nutmeg. Most liverwurst varieties are spreadable. Liverwurst is sold ready to eat, but it can be cooked further as well.

Childs.Title: LYONER
Childs.Definition: A German-type of pork sausage which is usually eaten cold

Childs.Title: MERGUEZ
Childs.Definition: Merguez is a red, spicy sausage from Algeria and Tunisia, North Africa. Merguez is flavoured with a wide range of spices, such as sumac for tartness, and paprika, cayenne pepper, or harissa, a hot chili paste, that gives it a red color. It is traditionally made fresh and eaten after grilling.

Childs.Title: MET(T)WURST
Childs.Definition: Mettwurst is a strongly flavoured German sausage made from raw minced meat, which is preserved by curing and smoking. The most common variety is soft and somewhat smoked but still soft and spreadable.

Childs.Title: MORTADELLA
Childs.Definition: Mortadella is a large Italian-type sausage or cold cut sausage made of finely hashed/ground heat-cured pork, which incorporates at least 15% small cubes of pork fat (principally the hard fat from the neck of the pig). It is delicately flavored with spices, including whole or ground black pepper, myrtle berries, nutmeg, coriander and pistachios and/or olives. In several Arab and Muslim countries, Mortadella is made from chicken, beef, or turkey.

Childs.Title: SALAMI
Childs.Definition: Salami is a cured sausage, fermented and air-dried, which can be stored at room temperature for periods of up to a year. Well known are Italian Salami, Hungarian Szalámi and Spanish Salchichón. Salami is cured in warm, humid conditions in order to encourage growth of the bacteria involved in the fermentation process. After fermentation,the sausage has to be dried.

Childs.Title: STRASBOURG
Childs.Definition: Strasbourg sausage is a mixture of lean meat of beef and pork emulsified stuffed in a casing of lamb with the unique seasoning.

Childs.Title: TEEWURST
Childs.Definition: Teewurst is a German sausage made from two parts of raw pork (and sometimes beef) and one part bacon, which are minced, seasoned, and typically packed in porous, artificial casings before being smoked over beech wood. The sausage is then aged for seven to ten days in order to develop its typical taste. Teewurst contains 30 to 40 percent fat, which makes it particularly easy to spread.

Childs.Title: THURINGER
Childs.Definition: A sausage from the German state of Thuringia made from finely minced pork, beef, or veal. It is seasoned with salt, pepper, caraway, marjoram, and garlic. Normally it is smoked and cured.

Childs.Title: UNCLASSIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unable to be classified within their specific market; e.g. goat's cheese - goat's cheeses is often generically labelled and cannot be further classified.

Childs.Title: UNIDENTIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unidentifiable given existing or available product information.

Childs.Title: WEISSWURST
Childs.Definition: Weisswurst is a traditional Bavarian sausage made from very finely minced meat and fresh bacon. It is an unsmoked sausage usually flavoured with parsley, lemon, mace, onions, ginger and cardamom. For consumption, the sausages are quickly boiled in water, resulting in a greyish-white colour when served.

Childs.Title: WIENER/VIENNA/FRANKFURTER (WURSTEL)/HOT DOG
Childs.Definition: A moist sausage of soft, even texture and flavor, often made from mechanically recovered meat or meat slurry. Most types are cured or sometimes smoked and may have the casing removed after the cooking process. Hot dogs are sold fully cooked and ready to eat, although they are usually warmed before serving.

Childs.Title: Pork Sausages - Prepared/Processed
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as a food made from ground pork, which may be prepared using a specific, regionally based process. The ground meat is mixed with other ingredients such as animal fat, salt, spices, herbs, vegetables or fruit and then typically packed in a casing, which may be link shaped or form a rope or ring, or sold without a casing such as bologna and some frankfurters. Some sausages are cooked during processing and may be preserved by curing, drying in cool air, or smoking.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as vegetarian sausages made from meat substitutes as well as pate.

Childs.Definition: Product was harvested from wild populations.

Childs.Title: Type of Sausage
Childs.Definition: Indicates, with reference to the product branding, labelling or packaging, the descriptive term that is used by the product manufacturer to identify the type of sausage.

Childs.Title: ANDOUILLE
Childs.Definition: A spiced, heavily smoked pork sausage, distinguished in some varieties by its use of the entire gastrointestinal system of the pig.

Childs.Title: ASPIC PRODUCT
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe products that are set in aspic or a savoury gelatine, this excludes head cheese.

Childs.Title: BIERSCHINKEN/KRAKAUER
Childs.Definition: Bierschinken is a scalded sausage from a cured mixture of meat, lard and spices that incorporates at least 15% small cubes of pork fat or cooked ham. It is produced mainly in Germany and Austria.

Childs.Title: BLOOD SAUSAGE/BLACK PUDDING/BLOOD PUDDING
Childs.Definition: Blood sausage is made by cooking blood with a filler until it is thick enough to congeal when cooled. Typical fillers include meat, fat, suet, bread, sweet potato, barley and oatmeal, and different meat sources are used.

Childs.Title: BOCKWURST
Childs.Definition: A German-style sausage made from ground veal and pork, flavored with salt, white pepper and paprika.

Childs.Title: BOEREWORS
Childs.Definition: Boerewors is a South African sausage made from coarsely minced beef, sometimes combined with minced pork, lamb, or both and spices such as coriander seed, black pepper, nutmeg, cloves and allspice. The sausage is preserved with salt and vinegar and packed in sausage casings. Traditional boerewors is usually formed into a continuous spiral. It can also be dried into what is colloquially known as droe wors.

Childs.Title: BOLOGNA
Childs.Definition: Bologna is an American-style sausage similar to Italian mortadella that can be made out of either chicken, turkey, beef, or pork. It is finely chopped or ground and contains lard, but without any visible pieces of fat. It is packed into casings with a variety of shapes including ring, chub, loaf, or rope. It is cooked, sometimes smoked, and sold with the casing removed and ready to eat.

Childs.Title: BRATWURST
Childs.Definition: Bratwurst is a sausage composed of several kinds of finely chopped meat that is traditionally prepared by grilling.

Childs.Title: CERVELAT
Childs.Definition: Cervelat is a cooked sausage consisting of a mixture of different meat, bacon, and pork rind that is packed into zebu intestines, slightly smoked and then boiled. It is produced mainly in Switzerland and in parts of Germany.

Childs.Title: CHORIZO/CHOURICO/LONGANIZA
Childs.Definition: Chorizo is typically a fermented, cured, smoked sausage that has a distinctive smokiness and deep red color from dried, smoked red peppers. Chorizo originates from the Iberian Peninsula.

Childs.Title: COUNTRY/BREAKFAST
Childs.Definition: Country and breakfast sausage is made from whole muscle product that is fresh and not cured or smoked (also known as "Whole Hog" sausage). It is normally made from pork but sometimes from turkey or beef. It is chopped and packed into casings for links or shaped as patties and used as part of a traditional American breakfast cuisine.

Childs.Title: EXTRAWURST
Childs.Definition: Extrawurst is an finely emulsified sausage, commonly of Austrian or German origin, with added bacon, garlic, spices and often potato added as a starch. It is cooked and served cold.

Childs.Title: FIGATELLI
Childs.Definition: Figatelli Sausage is a long, thin, highly flavored smoked pork liver sausage from Corsica.

Childs.Title: FLEISCHWURST
Childs.Definition: A German-type of pork sausage

Childs.Title: HEAD CHEESE
Childs.Definition: Head cheese is not a dairy cheese, but a terrine or meat jelly made with flesh from the head of a calf or pig, or less commonly a sheep or cow, and often set in aspic.

Childs.Title: ITALIAN SAUSAGE
Childs.Definition: A popular American-style sausage with traditional flavors and spices of Italy (fennel and/or anise). It is typically made from pork but sometimes from turkey or beef. Normally it is fresh but can be smoked. It is chopped and packed into casings for links, shaped as patties, or sold in loose bulk and used for stuffing, fillings and meat balls.

Childs.Title: JAGDWURST
Childs.Definition: A German cooked sausage made of lean beef and pork.

Childs.Title: KIELBASA
Childs.Definition: A traditional seasoned and gently smoked Polish sausage made from choice cuts of pork, and often mixed with a little beef or veal.

Childs.Title: KNOCKWURST
Childs.Definition: A short, plump sausage made from ground veal and pork with fresh garlic in hog casings. Aged over burning oak wood.

Childs.Title: LINGUICA
Childs.Definition: A Portuguese-style cured pork sausage seasoned with onions, garlic, and paprika.

Childs.Title: LIVERWURST/LIVER SAUSAGE/BRAUNSWEIGER
Childs.Definition: Liverwurst is a sausage containing about 10 to 20% liver, which gives a distinctive liver taste. Other ingredients are meat, fat, and spices such as ground black pepper, marjoram, allspice, thyme, ground mustard or nutmeg. Most liverwurst varieties are spreadable. Liverwurst is sold ready to eat, but it can be cooked further as well.

Childs.Title: LYONER
Childs.Definition: A German-type of pork sausage which is usually eaten cold

Childs.Title: MERGUEZ
Childs.Definition: Merguez is a red, spicy sausage from Algeria and Tunisia, North Africa. Merguez is flavoured with a wide range of spices, such as sumac for tartness, and paprika, cayenne pepper, or harissa, a hot chili paste, that gives it a red color. It is traditionally made fresh and eaten after grilling.

Childs.Title: MET(T)WURST
Childs.Definition: Mettwurst is a strongly flavoured German sausage made from raw minced meat, which is preserved by curing and smoking. The most common variety is soft and somewhat smoked but still soft and spreadable.

Childs.Title: MONTBELIARD
Childs.Definition: Montbéliard Sausage, from the city of Montbéliard, is made with local pork meat and smoked over saw dust.

Childs.Title: MORTADELLA
Childs.Definition: Mortadella is a large Italian-type sausage or cold cut sausage made of finely hashed/ground heat-cured pork, which incorporates at least 15% small cubes of pork fat (principally the hard fat from the neck of the pig). It is delicately flavored with spices, including whole or ground black pepper, myrtle berries, nutmeg, coriander and pistachios and/or olives. In several Arab and Muslim countries, Mortadella is made from chicken, beef, or turkey.

Childs.Title: MORTEAU
Childs.Definition: Morteau Sausage, also known as the Belle de Morteau, is a pork sausage traditional smoked pork sausage from the Morteau region of France (Haut-Doubs). It is a very strongly flavoured and very dense uncooked sausage. This sausage is smoked for at least 48 hours using sawdust made from conifer and juniper plants. It is not cooked, however, as the combustion is accompanied by a strong current of air. It is usually identifiable by the wooden peg/plug which is closing one of its end and sometimes with an escutcheon with the name of the manufacturer.

Childs.Title: SALAMI
Childs.Definition: Salami is a cured sausage, fermented and air-dried, which can be stored at room temperature for periods of up to a year. Well known are Italian Salami, Hungarian Szalámi and Spanish Salchichón. Salami is cured in warm, humid conditions in order to encourage growth of the bacteria involved in the fermentation process. After fermentation,the sausage has to be dried.

Childs.Title: TEEWURST
Childs.Definition: Teewurst is a German sausage made from two parts of raw pork (and sometimes beef) and one part bacon, which are minced, seasoned, and typically packed in porous, artificial casings before being smoked over beech wood. The sausage is then aged for seven to ten days in order to develop its typical taste. Teewurst contains 30 to 40 percent fat, which makes it particularly easy to spread.

Childs.Title: THURINGER
Childs.Definition: A sausage from the German state of Thuringia made from finely minced pork, beef, or veal. It is seasoned with salt, pepper, caraway, marjoram, and garlic. Normally it is smoked and cured.

Childs.Title: TOULOUSE
Childs.Definition: Toulouse sausage is a French sausage made with pork.

Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unidentifiable given existing or available product information.

Childs.Title: WEISSWURST
Childs.Definition: Weisswurst is a traditional Bavarian sausage made from very finely minced meat and fresh bacon. It is an unsmoked sausage usually flavoured with parsley, lemon, mace, onions, ginger and cardamom. For consumption, the sausages are quickly boiled in water, resulting in a greyish-white colour when served.

Childs.Title: WIENER/VIENNA/FRANKFURTER (WURSTEL)/HOT DOG
Childs.Definition: A moist sausage of soft, even texture and flavor, often made from mechanically recovered meat or meat slurry. Most types are cured or sometimes smoked and may have the casing removed after the cooking process. Hot dogs are sold fully cooked and ready to eat, although they are usually warmed before serving.

Childs.Title: Turkey Sausages - Prepared/Processed
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as a food made from ground turkey meat, which may be prepared using a specific, regionally based process. The ground meat is mixed with other ingredients such as animal fat, salt, spices, herbs, vegetables or fruit and then typically packed in a casing, which may be link shaped or form a rope or ring, or sold without a casing such as bologna and some frankfurters. Some sausages are cooked during processing and may be preserved by curing, drying in cool air, or smoking.

Childs.Title: PATTY

Childs.Title: ROPE/RING

Childs.Title: DRY AGED

Childs.Title: SEASONING

Childs.Title: Refrigeration State

Childs.Title: BULK FROZEN
Childs.Definition: Product is frozen after packaging and maintained at not less than -12.0 °C or more than -2.0 °C at all times after freezing.

Childs.Title: CHILLED
Childs.Definition: Product maintained at not less than -2.0 °C or more than + 4.0 °C at all times following the post-slaughter chilling process.

Childs.Title: INDIVIDUALLY FROZEN WITH ICE GLAZING
Childs.Definition: Product pieces are individually frozen before packaging and maintained at -18 °C or less at all times after freezing. Product is misted at the start of the freezing process to create a glaze of ice to keep pieces from sticking together and to minimize freezer burn.

Childs.Title: INDIVIDUALLY FROZEN WITHOUT ICE GLAZING
Childs.Definition: Product pieces are individually frozen before packaging and maintained at -18 °C or less at all times after freezing.

Childs.Title: SHELF STABLE
Childs.Definition: Product does not require refrigeration to maintain quality.

For consumption, the sausages are quickly boiled in water, resulting in a greyish-white colour when served.

Childs.Title: WIENER/VIENNA/FRANKFURTER (WURSTEL)/HOT DOG
Childs.Definition: A moist sausage of soft, even texture and flavor, often made from mechanically recovered meat or meat slurry. Most types are cured or sometimes smoked and may have the casing removed after the cooking process. Hot dogs are sold fully cooked and ready to eat, although they are usually warmed before serving.

Childs.Title: Veal Sausages - Prepared/Processed
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as a food made from ground veal, which may be prepared using a specific, regionally based process. The ground meat is mixed with other ingredients such as animal fat, salt, spices, herbs, vegetables or fruit and then typically packed in a casing, which may be link shaped or form a rope or ring, or sold without a casing such as bologna and some frankfurters. Some sausages are cooked during processing and may be preserved by curing, drying in cool air, or smoking.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as vegetarian sausages made from meat substitutes as well as pate.

Childs.Title: PATTY

Childs.Title: ROPE/RING

Childs.Title: BULK FROZEN
Childs.Definition: Product is frozen after packaging and maintained at not less than -12.0 °C or more than -2.0 °C at all times after freezing.

Childs.Title: CHILLED
Childs.Definition: Product maintained at not less than -2.0 °C or more than + 4.0 °C at all times following the post-slaughter chilling process.

Childs.Title: INDIVIDUALLY FROZEN WITH ICE GLAZING
Childs.Definition: Product pieces are individually frozen before packaging and maintained at -18 °C or less at all times after freezing. Product is misted at the start of the freezing process to create a glaze of ice to keep pieces from sticking together and to minimize freezer burn.

Childs.Title: INDIVIDUALLY FROZEN WITHOUT ICE GLAZING
Childs.Definition: Product pieces are individually frozen before packaging and maintained at -18 °C or less at all times after freezing.

Childs.Title: SHELF STABLE

Childs.Title: ANDOUILLE
Childs.Definition: A spiced, heavily smoked pork sausage, distinguished in some varieties by its use of the entire gastrointestinal system of the pig.

Childs.Title: ASPIC PRODUCT
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe products that are set in aspic or a savoury gelatine, this excludes head cheese.

Childs.Title: BIERSCHINKEN/KRAKAUER
Childs.Definition: Bierschinken is a scalded sausage from a cured mixture of meat, lard and spices that incorporates at least 15% small cubes of pork fat or cooked ham. It is produced mainly in Germany and Austria.

Childs.Title: BLOOD SAUSAGE/BLACK PUDDING/BLOOD PUDDING
Childs.Definition: Blood sausage is made by cooking blood with a filler until it is thick enough to congeal when cooled. Typical fillers include meat, fat, suet, bread, sweet potato, barley and oatmeal, and different meat sources are used.

Childs.Title: BOCKWURST
Childs.Definition: A German-style sausage made from ground veal and pork, flavored with salt, white pepper and paprika.

Childs.Title: BOEREWORS
Childs.Definition: Boerewors is a South African sausage made from coarsely minced beef, sometimes combined with minced pork, lamb, or both and spices such as coriander seed, black pepper, nutmeg, cloves and allspice. The sausage is preserved with salt and vinegar and packed in sausage casings. Traditional boerewors is usually formed into a continuous spiral. It can also be dried into what is colloquially known as droe wors.

Childs.Title: BOLOGNA
Childs.Definition: Bologna is an American-style sausage similar to Italian mortadella that can be made out of either chicken, turkey, beef, or pork. It is finely chopped or ground and contains lard, but without any visible pieces of fat. It is packed into casings with a variety of shapes including ring, chub, loaf, or rope. It is cooked, sometimes smoked, and sold with the casing removed and ready to eat.

Childs.Title: BRATWURST
Childs.Definition: Bratwurst is a sausage composed of several kinds of finely chopped meat that is traditionally prepared by grilling.

Childs.Title: CERVELAT
Childs.Definition: Cervelat is a cooked sausage consisting of a mixture of different meat, bacon, and pork rind that is packed into zebu intestines, slightly smoked and then boiled. It is produced mainly in Switzerland and in parts of Germany.

Childs.Title: CHORIZO/CHOURICO/LONGANIZA
Childs.Definition: Chorizo is typically a fermented, cured, smoked sausage that has a distinctive smokiness and deep red color from dried, smoked red peppers. Chorizo originates from the Iberian Peninsula.

Childs.Title: COUNTRY/BREAKFAST
Childs.Definition: Country and breakfast sausage is made from whole muscle product that is fresh and not cured or smoked (also known as "Whole Hog" sausage). It is normally made from pork but sometimes from turkey or beef. It is chopped and packed into casings for links or shaped as patties and used as part of a traditional American breakfast cuisine.

Childs.Title: EXTRAWURST
Childs.Definition: Extrawurst is an finely emulsified sausage, commonly of Austrian or German origin, with added bacon, garlic, spices and often potato added as a starch. It is cooked and served cold.

Childs.Title: FLEISCHWURST
Childs.Definition: A German-type of pork sausage

Childs.Title: ITALIAN SAUSAGE
Childs.Definition: A popular American-style sausage with traditional flavors and spices of Italy (fennel and/or anise). It is typically made from pork but sometimes from turkey or beef. Normally it is fresh but can be smoked. It is chopped and packed into casings for links, shaped as patties, or sold in loose bulk and used for stuffing, fillings and meat balls.

Childs.Title: JAGDWURST
Childs.Definition: A German cooked sausage made of lean beef and pork.

Childs.Title: KIELBASA
Childs.Definition: A traditional seasoned and gently smoked Polish sausage made from choice cuts of pork, and often mixed with a little beef or veal.

Childs.Title: KNOCKWURST
Childs.Definition: A short, plump sausage made from ground veal and pork with fresh garlic in hog casings. Aged over burning oak wood.

Childs.Title: LINGUICA
Childs.Definition: A Portuguese-style cured pork sausage seasoned with onions, garlic, and paprika.

Childs.Title: LIVERWURST/LIVER SAUSAGE/BRAUNSWEIGER
Childs.Definition: Liverwurst is a sausage containing about 10 to 20% liver, which gives a distinctive liver taste. Other ingredients are meat, fat, and spices such as ground black pepper, marjoram, allspice, thyme, ground mustard or nutmeg. Most liverwurst varieties are spreadable. Liverwurst is sold ready to eat, but it can be cooked further as well.

Childs.Title: LYONER
Childs.Definition: A German-type of pork sausage which is usually eaten cold

Childs.Title: MERGUEZ
Childs.Definition: Merguez is a red, spicy sausage from Algeria and Tunisia, North Africa. Merguez is flavoured with a wide range of spices, such as sumac for tartness, and paprika, cayenne pepper, or harissa, a hot chili paste, that gives it a red color. It is traditionally made fresh and eaten after grilling.

Childs.Title: MET(T)WURST
Childs.Definition: Mettwurst is a strongly flavoured German sausage made from raw minced meat, which is preserved by curing and smoking. The most common variety is soft and somewhat smoked but still soft and spreadable.

Childs.Title: MORTADELLA
Childs.Definition: Mortadella is a large Italian-type sausage or cold cut sausage made of finely hashed/ground heat-cured pork, which incorporates at least 15% small cubes of pork fat (principally the hard fat from the neck of the pig). It is delicately flavored with spices, including whole or ground black pepper, myrtle berries, nutmeg, coriander and pistachios and/or olives. In several Arab and Muslim countries, Mortadella is made from chicken, beef, or turkey.

Childs.Title: SALAMI
Childs.Definition: Salami is a cured sausage, fermented and air-dried, which can be stored at room temperature for periods of up to a year. Well known are Italian Salami, Hungarian Szalámi and Spanish Salchichón. Salami is cured in warm, humid conditions in order to encourage growth of the bacteria involved in the fermentation process. After fermentation,the sausage has to be dried.

Childs.Title: TEEWURST
Childs.Definition: Teewurst is a German sausage made from two parts of raw pork (and sometimes beef) and one part bacon, which are minced, seasoned, and typically packed in porous, artificial casings before being smoked over beech wood. The sausage is then aged for seven to ten days in order to develop its typical taste. Teewurst contains 30 to 40 percent fat, which makes it particularly easy to spread.

Childs.Title: THURINGER
Childs.Definition: A sausage from the German state of Thuringia made from finely minced pork, beef, or veal. It is seasoned with salt, pepper, caraway, marjoram, and garlic. Normally it is smoked and cured.

Childs.Title: SPREAD

Childs.Title: STICK

Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unidentifiable given existing or available product information.

Childs.Title: Cheese Substitutes (Perishable)
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as food made from non-dairy products, separated from the whey, sometimes fermented, and usually pressed, cooked, smoked, matured, or heated and mixed with artificial ingredients, such as emulsifiers, colourings and flavourings. These products must be refrigerated to extend their consumable life. These products can be with added ingredients, such as herbs and nuts, in blocks, rolls, slices, grated, cubes, spreadable and portions.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes products such as Frozen, Shelf Stable and Perishable Cheeses, and Shelf Stable and Frozen Cheese Substitutes and Cheese-Based/Flavoured Meals.

Childs.Title: Firmness of Cheese Substitute

Childs.Title: Formation
Childs.Definition: Indicates, with reference to the product branding, labelling or packaging, the descriptive term that is used by the product manufacturer to identify the state in which the product is sold.

Childs.Title: BLOCK
Childs.Definition: A trade item is referred to as a "block" when it has been formed or shaped into a larger geometric shape than what would be used for a serving or use. It is intended that the user would cut, slice, or otherwise separate portions of the item for individual consumption or use.

Childs.Title: CHUNKS
Childs.Definition: A trade item is referred to as "chunks" when it has been broken up into medium or larger pieces of irregular shape.

Childs.Title: CRUMBLES
Childs.Definition: A trade item is referred to as "crumbled" when it has been broken up into medium or smaller sized pieces of irregular shape.

Childs.Title: CUBE
Childs.Definition: A trade item is referred to as "cubed" when it has been cut into small to medium sized squares or rectangles.

Childs.Title: GRATED
Childs.Definition: A trade item is referred to as "grated" when it has been ground into a more granular form.

Childs.Title: INDIVIDUALLY FORMED SLICES
Childs.Definition: A trade item is referred to as "individually formed slices" when it has been formed as slices.

Childs.Title: SHAVED
Childs.Definition: A trade item is referred to as "shaved" if the loose particles are in the form of flat pieces larger than what would be termed shredded, but not as uniform as sliced.

Childs.Title: SHREDDED
Childs.Definition: Pulled product that is further size-reduced. A trade item is referred to as "shredded" if the loose particles are in the form of cylinders, shreds, or strings.

Childs.Title: SLICED
Childs.Definition: A trade item is referred to as "sliced" when it has been sliced.

Childs.Title: SPREAD
Childs.Definition: A trade item is referred to as "spread" if it has been formulated in such a fashion as to be easily smoothed out onto another item. Examples are butter, or cream cheese.

Childs.Title: STICK
Childs.Definition: A trade item is referred to as a "stick" if the solid item has been cut or formed in to individual strips. Even in the stick state the item is still a solid product. Specifically excludes products which may appear as a stick but are classified as strings .

Childs.Title: STRING
Childs.Definition: A trade item is referred to as a "string" if the item has been cut or formed in to individual strips which when separated form or appear to be strings. While in its combined state, the item may appear to be a stick, but it is when the item is separated or consumed it takes on the string state. Specifically excludes products which may appear as a stick but are classified as sticks.

Childs.Title: WEDGED

Childs.Title: WHEEL
Childs.Definition: A trade item is referred to as "wheel" when it has been formed in a round shape resembling a wheel or circle.

Childs.Definition: Clotted cream has the highest fat percentage of all creams. It is made by baking double cream until a delicious crust forms on the surface.

Childs.Title: CONDENSED CREAM
Childs.Definition: Condensed cream is cream from which water has been removed.

Childs.Title: CRÈME FRAICHE
Childs.Definition: Créme fraîche is similar to soured cream but with a milder taste. It is traditionally made from unpasteurised cream that has been left to ferment, but nowadays, pasteurised cream is thickened and soured with the addition of bacteria.

Childs.Title: HALF AND HALF
Childs.Definition: Half & Half is a mixture of cream & milk.

Childs.Title: HEAVY SOUR CREAM
Childs.Definition: Heavy sour cream is a dairy product produced by souring heavy cream (e.g. Schmand).

Childs.Title: SOUR CREAM
Childs.Definition: Soured cream has been treated with lactic acid, which gives it a tangy taste. It has a thick texture. Use it for making cheesecakes, dips, topping nachos, and in soups and sauces.

Childs.Definition: Used in the production of ice cream as a source of solids, in processed sliced cheese to increase viscosity, as an emulsifier in chocolate products and in dry mixes such as pancake mix, to add dairy flavor and enhance food browning.

Childs.Title: CASEIN
Childs.Definition: The name for a family of related phosphoproteins (αS1, αS2, β, κ). These proteins are commonly found in mammalian milk, making up 80% of the proteins incow milk and between 20% and 45% of the proteins in human milk.

Childs.Title: MILK SKIN
Childs.Definition: A sticky film of protein that forms on top of milk and milk-containing liquids (such as hot chocolate and some soups). It is caused by the denaturation of proteins such as casein.

Childs.Title: VACCENIC ACID
Childs.Definition: An omega-7 fatty acid. It is a naturally occurring trans-fatty acid found in the fat of ruminants and in dairy products such as milk, butter, and yogurt.

Childs.Title: WHEY
Childs.Definition: The liquid remaining after milk has been curdled and strained. It is a by-product of the manufacture of cheese or casein and has several commercial uses.

Childs.Title: WHEY PROTEIN
Childs.Definition: A mixture of globular proteins isolated from whey, the liquid material created as a by-product of cheese production.

Childs.Title: Eggs Extracts
Childs.Definition: Includes any products that can be described/observed as fractions of a component of a bird egg for use in the pharmaceutical, cosmetic or food industry. Typical egg extracts are substances such as lysozyme, avidin, vitamins and lipids.
Childs.DefinitionExcludes: Excludes imitation eggs and all other eggs in shell.

Childs.Definition: Egg is stored for an extended period of time without refrigeration or chemically treated to radically change the internal characteristics of the egg.

Childs.Title: CHEMICALLY EXTRACTED (EGG)
Childs.Definition: Product such as a protein or vitamin is isolated from a liquid egg product using acceptable food-grade processing aides.

Childs.Title: CONCENTRATED (EGG)
Childs.Definition: Water is removed using membrane technology.

Childs.Title: DRIED - PAN (EGG)
Childs.Definition: Liquid egg product is passed over a heated surface to evaporate water.

Childs.Title: DRIED - PROCESS UNIDENTIFIED (EGG)
Childs.Definition: Liquid egg product is converted to a dry form using an unknown process.

Childs.Title: DRIED - SPRAY (EGG)

Childs.Title: FERMENTED (EGG)

Childs.Title: FREEZE - DRIED (EGG)

Childs.Title: Ready-Made Combination Meals - Ready to Eat (Perishable)
Childs.Definition: Ready-made combination meal or microwave meal is a pre-packaged perishable full meal.  The meal requires no preparation, but may be warmed,  and contains all the elements typically contained in a single-serving meal.  A ready-made meal (also known as a TV Dinner) must have a main component and at least one additional component such as a side item, a dessert and/or beverage. These products must be refrigerated to extend their consumable life.

Childs.Title: Quality (UNECE Standard)
Childs.Definition: Indicates, with reference to the product branding, labelling or packaging, the descriptive term that is used by the product manufacturer to identify the quality classification or category according to Codex Alimentarius or UNECE standards. UNCLASSIFIED applies to fruits that are not yet packed (e.g. delivery of a grower to a pack house) or not qualified to be sold as fresh fruits in the target market since they do not meet the specifications required by legislation.

Childs.Title: "EXTRA" CLASS
Childs.Definition: Products in this class must be of superior quality. They must be characteristic of the variety and/or commercial type specified. Depending on the nature of the produce specific provisions can apply as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. They must be free from defects, with the exception of very slight superficial defects, provided these do not affect the general appearance of the produce, the quality, the keeping quality and presentation in the package.

Childs.Title: CLASS I
Childs.Definition: Products in this class must be of good quality. They must be characteristic of the variety and/or commercial type. There can be specific provisions, depending on the nature of the produce as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. Slight defects, however, may be allowed, provided these do not affect the general appearance of the produce, the quality, the keeping quality and presentation in the package:- a slight defect in shape- slight defects in colouring- slight skin defects.

Childs.Title: CLASS II
Childs.Definition: This class includes products that do not qualify for inclusion in a higher classes but satisfy the minimum requirements for this product as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. The following defects may be allowed, provided the produce retain their essential characteristics as regards the quality, the keeping quality and presentation:- defects in shape- defects in colouring- skin defects.

Childs.Title: "EXTRA" CLASS
Childs.Definition: Products in this class must be of superior quality. They must be characteristic of the variety and/or commercial type specified. Depending on the nature of the produce specific provisions can apply as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. They must be free from defects, with the exception of very slight superficial defects, provided these do not affect the general appearance of the produce, the quality, the keeping quality and presentation in the package.

Childs.Title: CLASS I
Childs.Definition: Products in this class must be of good quality. They must be characteristic of the variety and/or commercial type. There can be specific provisions, depending on the nature of the produce as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. Slight defects, however, may be allowed, provided these do not affect the general appearance of the produce, the quality, the keeping quality and presentation in the package:- a slight defect in shape- slight defects in colouring- slight skin defects.

Childs.Title: CLASS II
Childs.Definition: This class includes products that do not qualify for inclusion in a higher classes but satisfy the minimum requirements for this product as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. The following defects may be allowed, provided the produce retain their essential characteristics as regards the quality, the keeping quality and presentation:- defects in shape- defects in colouring- skin defects.

UNCLASSIFIED applies to fruits that are not yet packed (e.g. delivery of a grower to a pack house) or not qualified to be sold as fresh fruits in the target market since they do not meet the specifications required by legislation.

Childs.Title: "EXTRA" CLASS
Childs.Definition: Products in this class must be of superior quality. They must be characteristic of the variety and/or commercial type specified. Depending on the nature of the produce specific provisions can apply as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. They must be free from defects, with the exception of very slight superficial defects, provided these do not affect the general appearance of the produce, the quality, the keeping quality and presentation in the package.

Childs.Title: CLASS I
Childs.Definition: Products in this class must be of good quality. They must be characteristic of the variety and/or commercial type. There can be specific provisions, depending on the nature of the produce as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. Slight defects, however, may be allowed, provided these do not affect the general appearance of the produce, the quality, the keeping quality and presentation in the package:- a slight defect in shape- slight defects in colouring- slight skin defects.

Childs.Title: CLASS II
Childs.Definition: This class includes products that do not qualify for inclusion in a higher classes but satisfy the minimum requirements for this product as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. The following defects may be allowed, provided the produce retain their essential characteristics as regards the quality, the keeping quality and presentation:- defects in shape- defects in colouring- skin defects.

Childs.Title: UNCLASSIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unable to be classified within their specific market; e.g. goat's cheese - goat's cheeses is often generically labelled and cannot be further classified.

Childs.Title: UNIDENTIFIED
Childs.Definition: This term is used to describe those product attributes that are unidentifiable given existing or available product information.

Childs.Title: Quality (UNECE Standard)
Childs.Definition: Indicates, with reference to the product branding, labelling or packaging, the descriptive term that is used by the product manufacturer to identify the quality classification or category according to Codex Alimentarius or UNECE standards. UNCLASSIFIED applies to fruits that are not yet packed (e.g. delivery of a grower to a pack house) or not qualified to be sold as fresh fruits in the target market since they do not meet the specifications required by legislation.

Childs.Title: "EXTRA" CLASS
Childs.Definition: Products in this class must be of superior quality. They must be characteristic of the variety and/or commercial type specified. Depending on the nature of the produce specific provisions can apply as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. They must be free from defects, with the exception of very slight superficial defects, provided these do not affect the general appearance of the produce, the quality, the keeping quality and presentation in the package.

Childs.Title: CLASS I
Childs.Definition: Products in this class must be of good quality. They must be characteristic of the variety and/or commercial type. There can be specific provisions, depending on the nature of the produce as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. Slight defects, however, may be allowed, provided these do not affect the general appearance of the produce, the quality, the keeping quality and presentation in the package:- a slight defect in shape- slight defects in colouring- slight skin defects.

Childs.Title: CLASS II
Childs.Definition: This class includes products that do not qualify for inclusion in a higher classes but satisfy the minimum requirements for this product as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. The following defects may be allowed, provided the produce retain their essential characteristics as regards the quality, the keeping quality and presentation:- defects in shape- defects in colouring- skin defects.

Childs.Title: Quality (UNECE Standard)
Childs.Definition: Indicates, with reference to the product branding, labelling or packaging, the descriptive term that is used by the product manufacturer to identify the quality classification or category according to Codex Alimentarius or UNECE standards. UNCLASSIFIED applies to fruits that are not yet packed (e.g. delivery of a grower to a pack house) or not qualified to be sold as fresh fruits in the target market since they do not meet the specifications required by legislation.

Childs.Title: "EXTRA" CLASS
Childs.Definition: Products in this class must be of superior quality. They must be characteristic of the variety and/or commercial type specified. Depending on the nature of the produce specific provisions can apply as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. They must be free from defects, with the exception of very slight superficial defects, provided these do not affect the general appearance of the produce, the quality, the keeping quality and presentation in the package.

Childs.Title: CLASS I
Childs.Definition: Products in this class must be of good quality. They must be characteristic of the variety and/or commercial type. There can be specific provisions, depending on the nature of the produce as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. Slight defects, however, may be allowed, provided these do not affect the general appearance of the produce, the quality, the keeping quality and presentation in the package:- a slight defect in shape- slight defects in colouring- slight skin defects.

Childs.Title: CLASS II
Childs.Definition: This class includes products that do not qualify for inclusion in a higher classes but satisfy the minimum requirements for this product as specified in the UNECE Standards for Fresh Fruit and vegetables. The following defects may be allowed, provided the produce retain their essential characteristics as regards the quality, the keeping quality and presentation:- defects in shape- defects in colouring- skin defects.
